# Regras

Todas as regras do sistema, de todas as unidades. Cada uma leva ao texto na página da sua
camada.

Para ver uma camada inteira de uma vez — com a visão geral de cada unidade e os cenários —
abra a página dela em `camadas/`.

## apoio

### [BRCRB — BoardCards — reading the repository's board, where the work queue lives in github mode](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B01 — A card is on the board only when it carries every configured label and, when a state is asked, that state's label.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B02 — The owner of a card is its last comment starting with `anchors-owner:`; a card with no such comment has no owner.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B03 — A card labelled `needs-user` (or its Portuguese variant) is declined unless the agent declared it decides the product; any other card is never declined.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B04 — The agent's own card is the first card it owns that is in progress or in review and not declined, reported with its most advanced state label; a card it owns that is to-do or ready-to-review, or a card of another owner, is not its own work.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B05 — A unit's card is the one open card whose TITLE holds the code in brackets, in any case; the code in the body, or a longer code in brackets, does not count.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B06 — A card named by number is returned when it is open and carries every configured label.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B07 — Board queries through `gh api` never carry `--repo`; every other `gh` call names the repository.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-B08 — Asking for work dispatches the claim pipeline with the agent as its input.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E01 — The configured labels are empty.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E02 — The repository is not `owner/name`.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E03 — The unit code is empty or blank.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E04 — No open card has the code in its title.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E05 — Two or more open cards have the code in their title.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E06 — The card named by number is closed, or lacks a configured label.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

- [BRCRB-E07 — The comment body is empty or blank.](layers/apoio.md#brcrb--boardcards--reading-the-repositorys-board-where-the-work-queue-lives-in-github-mode)

### [CLWTC — ClaimWait — asking the claim pipeline for a card and waiting, bounded, for the answer](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B01 — An agent's claim runs are the runs titled `anchors · claim for <agent>`; another agent's runs never count as its own. (`ClaimRunTitle`)](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B02 — While one of the agent's runs is still pending, no claim is dispatched: the wait follows the oldest pending run.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B03 — The run the wait follows is the oldest run above every run of the agent that existed before; an older finished run is not its answer.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B04 — The wait returns as soon as the agent owns a card under way, having dispatched once.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B05 — When the followed run finishes, the board is looked at once more; with no card then, the wait ends with the run and without spending the timeout.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B06 — A cancelled run is dispatched again, at most twice, and only before the deadline; the last cancelled run is reported.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-B07 — The wait is bounded (three minutes by default, looking every five seconds): when the time runs out the outcome says so and names the pending run, without a second dispatch.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

- [CLWTC-E01 — The run list is not the expected JSON.](layers/apoio.md#clwtc--claimwait--asking-the-claim-pipeline-for-a-card-and-waiting-bounded-for-the-answer)

### [GHRNG — GhRunner — running `gh` for the board so that a failure names its cause and never waits for input](layers/apoio.md#ghrng--ghrunner--running-gh-for-the-board-so-that-a-failure-names-its-cause-and-never-waits-for-input)

- [GHRNG-B01 — `gh` runs with no input: a `gh` that reads its input gets its end at once instead of waiting.](layers/apoio.md#ghrng--ghrunner--running-gh-for-the-board-so-that-a-failure-names-its-cause-and-never-waits-for-input)

- [GHRNG-B02 — A `gh` that exits with code 4 fails with the hint that it is NOT AUTHENTICATED, that `gh auth login` fixes it, and that the login is interactive.](layers/apoio.md#ghrng--ghrunner--running-gh-for-the-board-so-that-a-failure-names-its-cause-and-never-waits-for-input)

- [GHRNG-B03 — Any other failure, another exit code or a command that could not start, carries no authentication hint.](layers/apoio.md#ghrng--ghrunner--running-gh-for-the-board-so-that-a-failure-names-its-cause-and-never-waits-for-input)

- [GHRNG-E01 — REF[GHRNG-B02]: `gh` without credentials is the failure B02 explains with its fix](layers/apoio.md#ghrng--ghrunner--running-gh-for-the-board-so-that-a-failure-names-its-cause-and-never-waits-for-input)

### [DCLND — DocLinks — the anchors, links, sizes and layer arrows the documentation templates are given](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B01 — `GitHubAnchor`: A heading's anchor is its text trimmed and lower-cased, keeping letters and digits (accented ones included), turning each space, hyphen and underscore into a hyphen, and dropping every other character.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B02 — A rule's link goes to its layer's page, at the rule's own heading when the layer is small and the rule is written as a heading, and at the heading of the unit that holds it when the layer is big or the rule is a table row or a bullet.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B09 — A layer's page (`layerPage`) is in the folder that holds the layer's template under `doct/`; with no template for the layer, in the folder of the project's language (`LayerDir`: `layers`, `camadas`, `capas`).](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B03 — A scenario's link goes to its layer's page, at the scenario's heading when the layer is small, at its unit's heading when the layer is big, and at the bare page when the layer is big and the scenario's spec is unknown.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B04 — The size of a selection counts its units, their rules, their spec lines and their scenarios, and is remembered per selection, so asking again returns the same answer and two selections never share one.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B05 — The size of a selection that matches no spec is zero, not an error, and such a selection is never big.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B06 — The arrows between layers are the map's `needs` and `depends-on` edges between two specs of different layers, one arrow per pair of layers carrying the number of edges behind it; edges of other types, edges touching a non-spec node and edges inside one layer are left out.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B07 — The arrows are ordered by source layer and then by target layer, so the diagram does not change shape between builds.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-B08 — `MermaidID`: A diagram node identifier is `n_` followed by the name with every character outside ASCII letters and digits replaced by an underscore.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-I01 — Every link the generated index writes resolves to a heading that exists on the page it points at, on a small layer and on a big one alike.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

- [DCLND-X01 — The unit does not decide what "big" means: it asks the layout decision, and the template function exposing it takes no threshold.](layers/apoio.md#dclnd--doclinks--the-anchors-links-sizes-and-layer-arrows-the-documentation-templates-are-given)

### [C4CNC — C4Containers — the declared containers, each with the units that run in it, for the architecture page](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-B01 — Each declared container carries the specs whose layer is one of the layers it declares, matched ignoring case and surrounding spaces, ordered by layer, then by code, then by path, so units with the same layer and code keep one order from build to build.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-B02 — The internal containers, the ones that get a level 3 diagram, are the declared containers minus those marked external.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-B03 — The orphan layers are the layers that have specs and that no container declares.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-B04 — Without a project configuration there are no containers and no orphan layers.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-I01 — Every layer that has specs is either held by a declared container or named among the orphan layers — never neither.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

- [C4CNC-X01 — The containers are only the declared ones: none is deduced from the map or the layers.](layers/apoio.md#c4cnc--c4containers--the-declared-containers-each-with-the-units-that-run-in-it-for-the-architecture-page)

### [DTCDC — DocTemplateCompiler — compiles documentation pages from templates that reference the specs' content](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B01 — A template that references a spec's section gets that section's text in the compiled page, not a link to the spec.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B02 — Every compiled page opens with the generated marker, naming the template's path from the project root and carrying a stamp of the page's inputs.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B03 — A page that already exists without the generated marker is never overwritten: it is left as is and reported as skipped.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B04 — A dry run compiles every template and writes nothing.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B05 — Templates in subfolders of `doct/` are compiled to the same relative path under `docs/`.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B06 — A spec's layer is the `layer:` line of its own header when it has one, and the map's layer otherwise.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B07 — The layers offered to templates are the distinct layers that have specs, sorted.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B08 — A section is the text under a second-level heading of that exact name, without the heading, up to the next second-level heading; deeper headings inside it do not end it, and a missing section is empty.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B09 — A rule written as a heading — a rule code, a dash and a title — has its body up to the next rule or second-level heading.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B11 — A section asked by a title the section catalog knows, and absent under that exact title, is the same section under its title in another language of the catalog (`Visão Geral` finds `Overview`); a title outside the catalog finds only itself.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B12 — A spec's rules are read in the three catalogued forms — heading, table row, bold bullet — with the map's rule definition; only the spec's own codes, each at its first definition, so a Rule uses row does not repeat a rule; a table row's title is the cell after the code and its body the cells after that, and only a heading rule is marked as having a heading of its own.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B10 — A rule's title carries no HTML comment, even one written on the heading line, while the title's words stay.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B13 — A spec header's `updated_at:` line, within the first ten lines, is not part of the stamp; the same line further down is content and is.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B14 — A page without the generated marker is never reported stale.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B17 — A page whose generated marker carries no stamp (compiled by an earlier version) is compared by its body below the marker line: stale when the body differs from today's compilation, fresh when it is the same.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B18 — A layer the project has — the Estrutura declares it, or the map has a file in it — and no spec declares selects nothing instead of failing, and `layerFiles` counts its files in the map, so the architecture page says the layer has no spec instead of the build aborting; a container whose layers have no spec lists them with their files.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B19 — A compiler built with a source reads the specs, the features, the compiled pages and the templates of the staleness shortcut through it — the git index, when a commit is checked —, and one built without reads the tree. (`NewWith`)](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B20 — A compiler built with a source compiles each template as the source holds it, and a template the source does not hold is not compiled: under the index, a template another session is editing is compiled as the commit records it. (`templates`, `compile`)](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B21 — `Compiled` returns the pages that are out of date, compiled, without writing them; a page up to date is not compiled, and a page written by hand is never among them. (`Compiled`)](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B15 — The uncovered specs are those no template selected while every template was compiled, sorted by path.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-B16 — `IsGenerated`, `IsHandwritten`: A page is recognised as generated by the generated marker on its first line, and as declared handwritten by the handwritten marker; a page with neither is neither.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-I01 — Right after a build, no page is stale.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-X01 — Asking which pages are stale never writes a page.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-X02 — The specs are those the map lists; a spec file on disk that the map does not know is not loaded.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E01 — A selection filter has no `=`, names a field other than `layer` or `code`, or matches no spec and names no layer of the project.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E02 — A template's selection fails during the build.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E03 — A template does not parse or does not execute.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E04 — `New`: A spec the map lists is not on disk.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E05 — The project has no `doct/` folder.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

- [DTCDC-E06 — A template asks for one spec by a code no spec has.](layers/apoio.md#dtcdc--doctemplatecompiler--compiles-documentation-pages-from-templates-that-reference-the-specs-content)

### [DCKND — DocKinds — what each kind of project documentation must answer, told to the agent that writes it](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-B01 — Each of the six known kinds (openapi, c4, schema, components, adr, runbook) has a title, a non-empty list of items the document must cover, and a trap.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-B02 — `InstructionFor`: The kind is looked up ignoring case and surrounding spaces, so ` OpenAPI ` finds the openapi instruction.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-B03 — An unknown kind gets a minimal instruction with no items and no trap, titled by the kind — or by the document's path when the kind is empty.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-B04 — `Duty`: The duty text is the title followed by the path in backticks, then the declared why when there is one, then one bulleted line per item, then the trap line when there is one — in that order.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-I01 — `KnownKinds`: The list of known kinds and the set of instructions are the same set: every listed kind has an instruction, and no instruction exists for a kind the list omits.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

- [DCKND-X01 — The unit never refuses a documentation kind.](layers/apoio.md#dcknd--dockinds--what-each-kind-of-project-documentation-must-answer-told-to-the-agent-that-writes-it)

### [DCOXX — DocLayout — the one decision of whether a documentation page shows everything or summarizes](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

- [DCOXX-B01 — A selection is big when its unit count is above the unit cut-off OR its line count is above the line cut-off; either one passing is enough.](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

- [DCOXX-B02 — `DefaultLayout`: The default cut-off, when the project declares none, is 20 units or 2000 lines.](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

- [DCOXX-B03 — The summary sentence is empty for a selection that is not big; for a big one it states the unit count, the rule count and both cut-offs, so the reader knows the page is a summary and where the full text is.](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

- [DCOXX-I01 — The cut-off is strict: a selection exactly at a limit is not big, one past it is.](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

- [DCOXX-X01 — The layout only answers "is this selection big"; it never splits a layer into several pages.](layers/apoio.md#dcoxx--doclayout--the-one-decision-of-whether-a-documentation-page-shows-everything-or-summarizes)

### [DCSCD — DocScaffolds — the starting templates `anchors docs init` proposes, one page per question and per layer](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B01 — `Scaffolds`: There are three fixed page templates — architecture, behaviour and rules — each with a template name, a body and a sentence saying what the page answers.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B02 — `ScaffoldLayer`: A layer's page template is named after the layer inside the layer folder of the project's language (`LayerDir`, DCLND-B09).](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B03 — Init writes the three fixed templates plus one layer page for each layer that has specs, each one opening with a template comment carrying the sentence of what the page answers.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B05 — `ScaffoldOpenAPI`: When a spec has an `Endpoint` section, init also writes `openapi.yaml.tmpl`, compiling the project's OpenAPI under the project folder's name and version `0.1.0`, for the team to edit.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B04 — An existing template is not rewritten unless forced; it is reported as skipped. Forced, it is rewritten.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B06 — On a big layer, the layer page carries the layout's summary sentence and each unit's overview and rule list, without the scenarios' steps.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B07 — The architecture page shows the protocol of every declared conversation, lists external containers at level 2, and gives a level 3 section to each internal container only.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B09 — The templates are in the project's language: their names (`architecture`, `arquitetura`, `arquitectura`…), what they show — headings, paragraphs, diagram labels, empty-state notes — and the section titles the layer page asks for, which are the language's titles in the section catalog; a language with no table gets English, and no template keeps an unfilled text. The notes to whoever edits a template are in English.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-B08 — When no container is declared, the architecture page says so instead of leaving empty diagrams.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-I01 — The skeleton init writes compiles with the compiler, producing one page per template written.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-X01 — Init only writes templates; it never writes a compiled page.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

- [DCSCD-E01 — The templates folder cannot be created or a template cannot be written.](layers/apoio.md#dcscd--docscaffolds--the-starting-templates-anchors-docs-init-proposes-one-page-per-question-and-per-layer)

### [GSRGH — GherkinScenarioReader — the scenarios of a unit's feature, with their steps, for the documentation](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B01 — A line opening with any scenario keyword of any Gherkin dialect, outlines included, followed by a colon, opens a scenario titled by the rest of the line; an examples table heading does not open one.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B02 — In the tag line above a scenario, the first tag shaped like a scenario code becomes the scenario's code, and every other tag goes to its tags without the `@`.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B03 — A scenario's body is its non-blank lines, as written, until the next scenario opens; blank lines are dropped.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B04 — A Feature, Background or Rule heading, in English or Portuguese, closes the current scenario, so its lines never join the scenario before it.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B05 — A spec's features are the feature nodes linked to it by a map edge in either direction, whatever their file names.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-B06 — The scenarios of a selection are those of every spec the selection filter picks, and a filter the spec selection refuses is refused here with the same error.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-I01 — Every scenario read for a spec carries that spec's code, so the documentation and the links know which unit it belongs to.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-X01 — The reader does not interpret the steps: the body is kept verbatim, indentation included.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-E01 — A feature the map links to the spec cannot be read from disk.](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

- [GSRGH-E02 — REF[GSRGH-B06]: a malformed or empty selection filter is refused with the spec selection's error, which fails the template that asked](layers/apoio.md#gsrgh--gherkinscenarioreader--the-scenarios-of-a-units-feature-with-their-steps-for-the-documentation)

### [FLGRF — FlagGrammar — the fixed grammar of a feature-flag scenario's condition](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-B01 — The symbolic, LaunchDarkly-style and Flagsmith/Unleash-style spellings of a comparison give the same operator, ignoring case, spaces, underscores and hyphens. (`Parse`)](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-B02 — The operand loses one layer of surrounding double or single quotes, and keeps any inner quotes.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-B03 — The absent and present cases, in their English forms or in the word the catalog gives in any supported language, compare against nothing and carry no operand.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-B04 — The longest operator wins: a two-character symbol before its one-character prefix, and the longest word prefix before a shorter one.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-B05 — Only the absent and present operators need no operand.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-X01 — Does not accept operators that evaluate against a flag service (segment match, modulo), nor prose.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-E01 — The condition is empty or blank.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-E02 — An operator has nothing to compare against.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

- [FLGRF-E03 — The condition is not a known comparison nor an absent/present word.](layers/apoio.md#flgrf--flaggrammar--the-fixed-grammar-of-a-feature-flag-scenarios-condition)

### [FLPRF — FlagParse — reading a project's flag files and the scenarios their values open](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B01 — The scenarios of a flag file are its table rows whose code carries the letter G, each with its code, its parsed condition and what holds then; rows of other letters are ignored. (`ParseFile`, `ParseContent`)](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B02 — The flag's code is the unit part of its first scenario code, and its name is the file name without `.flag.md`.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B03 — Each scenario records the line of the file it was read from.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B04 — A row whose condition the grammar refuses is kept as a scenario carrying the refusal.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B05 — A flag declares the absent case when one of its scenarios has the absent condition.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B06 — Loading a project reads every `.flag.md` in `flags/`, sorted by file name, and gives nothing, without error, when `flags/` does not exist.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-B07 — The scenarios of all flags can be indexed by their code. (`ByCode`)](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-E01 — REF[FLPRF-B04]: a condition the grammar refuses is the failure B04 keeps as a finding](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

- [FLPRF-E02 — `flags/` exists but cannot be read as a folder, or a flag file in it cannot be read.](layers/apoio.md#flprf--flagparse--reading-a-projects-flag-files-and-the-scenarios-their-values-open)

### [FLBLF — FlowBuild — assembling the work-flow graph from the project's flow and action files](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B01 — The graph is built from every `flows/actions/*.action.md` and then every `flows/*.flow.md`, each set sorted by file name; a project without flows gives no graph and no error.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B02 — A state is a heading carrying a code, recorded with its title and the file it comes from.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B03 — An exit is a bullet carrying a code in backticks; it belongs to the last state above it, and the rest of the line is its condition. An exit above every state is ignored.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B04 — A line carrying two codes routes a result: a transition from the current step, on the first code, to the second code.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B05 — A state is terminal only when its section declares `@terminal`.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B06 — The piece a step fits is read from its section's "fits" line, written with the keyword of any supported language; a step without one fits nothing.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B07 — The reaction a result suggests is read from its section's "suggests" line and recorded on the state, never as a transition; a result without one suggests nothing.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-B08 — The condition of a routed result is the prose of its line before, between and after the two codes, without the codes, their backticks, the arrow (`→` or `->`), the bullet and trailing punctuation.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

- [FLBLF-E01 — `flows/` or `flows/actions/` exists but cannot be read as a folder, or a flow or action file in them cannot be read.](layers/apoio.md#flblf--flowbuild--assembling-the-work-flow-graph-from-the-projects-flow-and-action-files)

### [FLMDF — FlowModel — the questions a work-flow graph answers: what comes next, and what is broken](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B01 — The exits of a state are exactly the transitions declared from it; a state with no exit has none. (`Next`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B02 — A state is found by its code, and a code with no state is not found. (`StateByCode`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B03 — The states of a flow come in the order its file declares them, never alphabetical, and the flows are listed once each in order of appearance. (`StatesOf`, `Flows`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B04 — The entry of a flow is its first declared step that is not a result; a file that declares only results has no entry. (`Entry`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B05 — A code is a result when the letter after its hyphen is the outcome letter, O (`config.OutcomeLetter`; it was R until format 5). (`IsResult`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B06 — The title of an action is the name of the action file that declares its results; an action nobody wrote has none. (`ActionTitle`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B07 — A step no transition reaches is unreachable, except the first state of each flow; results are never unreachable. (`Unreachable`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B08 — A result that no transition routes is unhandled. (`Unhandled`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-B09 — A transition to a state that does not exist is dangling. (`Dangling`)](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

- [FLMDF-X01 — A project without flows answers nothing to every question, and none of them fails.](layers/apoio.md#flmdf--flowmodel--the-questions-a-work-flow-graph-answers-what-comes-next-and-what-is-broken)

### [INCTA — I18nCatalog — every message a person reads, in the project's language, with a fallback that never goes blank](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B01 — The supported languages are pt-BR, en and es, and the default is en. (`IsSupported`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B02 — Setting an empty language sets the default. (`Current`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B03 — A message is resolved in the current language, with its arguments interpolated in every language.](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B04 — A key missing from the current language's catalog is resolved in the default language.](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B05 — A key missing from every catalog resolves to the key itself.](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B06 — The values of a key across all languages come back once each, in the order of the supported languages. (`AllTranslations`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B07 — A key can be resolved in a given language without changing the current one, and resolves to empty text when that language lacks it. (`TIn`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-B08 — A written section title gives back the key it realises and its language, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; a title that is not in the catalogs, or an empty one, gives nothing. (`SectionKeyFor`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-I01 — Every supported language has a non-empty catalog, and all catalogs hold exactly the same keys. (`Keys`)](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

- [INCTA-E01 — A language outside the supported list is set.](layers/apoio.md#incta--i18ncatalog--every-message-a-person-reads-in-the-projects-language-with-a-fallback-that-never-goes-blank)

### [LGSCL — LogScan — finding the occurrences of declared failures in the project's logs](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B01 — With no declared log path, nothing is scanned and no result is given.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B02 — Every file matching the declared paths is read, whatever its line format; each declared code found counts one occurrence per line, and the number of files and lines read is reported.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B03 — Only the `-E` codes the project's specs declare become occurrences; a code that merely looks like one is not captured.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B04 — A failure code no spec declares is reported apart with its count: with delimiters, whenever it is delimited; without delimiters, only on a line carrying a failure word (error, err, fatal, severe, critical, crit, panic, exception).](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B05 — The code is looked for between `#[` and `]` by default; a declared pair of delimiters replaces them, and an empty pair looks for the bare code.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B06 — A legacy alias binds its code to the lines its text pattern matches, only when the line carries no declared code.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B07 — With a timestamp pattern declared, each occurrence records the earliest and latest moment it was seen.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B08 — The occurrences come back sorted by rule code.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-B09 — The `-E` rules a spec catalogues are listed from its headings, table rows and bold bullets. (`SpecFailureCodes`)](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

- [LGSCL-E01 — A declared alias or timestamp is not a valid pattern.](layers/apoio.md#lgscl--logscan--finding-the-occurrences-of-declared-failures-in-the-projects-logs)

### [MGLTR — CodeLetters — rewriting the letter of the codes of one kind of unit](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

- [MGLTR-B01 — The letter renames of the steps between two formats are gathered in order; outside that interval none are (`LetterRenamesBetween`).](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

- [MGLTR-B02 — A code whose unit is of a renamed kind and whose letter is that kind's old one is rewritten to the new letter, keeping its unit and number (`RewriteCodeLetters`).](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

- [MGLTR-B03 — Every other code is left as it is: a unit of another kind or of no known kind, another letter of the same unit, and a code with more than two digits.](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

- [MGLTR-B04 — The rewrite reports, per code, how many times it was replaced, and the report is listed in a stable order (`SortedCounts`).](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

- [MGLTR-B05 — Rewriting a text already rewritten changes nothing.](layers/apoio.md#mgltr--codeletters--rewriting-the-letter-of-the-codes-of-one-kind-of-unit)

### [MGFLM — MigrateFile — takes one project file from its declared format to the current one, renaming only what is a key](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B01 — `FormatOf` answers that the file's format is the number in its top-level `version:` line; a file without that line is format 1.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B02 — `MigrateFile`: A file already at or above the target format is left untouched and reported as unchanged.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B03 — An old key is renamed only where it is a key at the start of a line — at any indentation, list items included — keeping its value; the same word in a comment or inside a value is not touched.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B04 — Each rename applies only to the file it was declared for: a key of the map is never renamed in the configuration file, nor the reverse.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B05 — A value is renamed only under the key the step names and only when the whole value matches an old name.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B06 — The steps are applied in order, each on the result of the previous, so a key renamed twice across formats ends under its latest name.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B07 — The `version:` line is raised to the target, even when no key or value changed.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B08 — A map or a configuration without a `version:` line gets one inserted right after its leading comment block.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B09 — The result counts each renamed key, and each renamed `key: value`, by its old form, and reports whether the text changed.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B10 — A dry run reports what would change, counts included, without writing the file.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B11 — A top-level `version:` line followed by a comment is read by its number, and raised in place keeping the comment.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-B12 — A file with CRLF line endings (a Windows checkout) is read and written as it is: its `version:` is found, a file at the target is left untouched, and a migrated file gets its `version:` stamped or inserted with `\r\n`, never a second one.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-I01 — Migrating twice is the same as migrating once: the second run changes nothing and reports no change.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-X01 — Does not load the file through the YAML parser: text the parser would refuse is still read and migrated.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-E01 — The file cannot be read.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-E02 — The top-level `version:` line holds something that is not a number (text such as `abc`, or a number too large to represent).](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

- [MGFLM-E03 — A step between the file's format and the target is missing.](layers/apoio.md#mgflm--migratefile--takes-one-project-file-from-its-declared-format-to-the-current-one-renaming-only-what-is-a-key)

### [MGSTM — MigrationSteps — the registered steps, one per format, take any project from format 1 to the current format](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B01 — Format 2 renames the map keys `gerado_por`, `code_declarado` and `julgamentos` to `generated_by`, `code_declared` and `judgments`, and the configuration key `trinca_opcional` to `triad_optional`.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B02 — Format 2 renames the Portuguese gate names to their English names as the value of `gate` in the map and of `name`, `id` and `check` in the configuration.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B03 — Format 3 renames the eight remaining Portuguese gate names — among them `regra-implementada` to `rule-implemented` and `header-conforme` to `header-valid` — as the value of `name` and `check` in the configuration.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B05 — Format 5 renames no key: it renames code letters by kind of unit — a plan's phase `F` to `W`, a flow's step `P` to `T`, a result `R` to `O`, of an action or of a flow fitted as a piece —, applied by the command over the project's files; a file migrated to 5 only gets the new `version:`.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B06 — Format 6 renames the gate `triad-complete` to `unit-complete` as the value of `gate` in the map and of `name`, `id` and `check` in the configuration, and the configuration key `optional_triad_edges` to `optional_unit_edges`.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-B04 — Format 4 renames the configuration keys `auto_judgment`, `triad_optional`, `requires_code` and `rule_marking` to `enable_auto_judgment`, `optional_triad_edges`, `sections_require_code` and `rule_marking_policy`.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-I01 — The registered steps form an unbroken chain from format 1 to the current format: each format has exactly one step, and every step says what it changed.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-I02 — A key renamed by several formats ends under its latest name: a configuration on format 1 with `trinca_opcional` ends with `optional_unit_edges`, keeping its value.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-X01 — Format 3 does not rename the map's `gate` values nor the configuration's `id` values.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

- [MGSTM-X02 — Format 4 renames nothing in the map.](layers/apoio.md#mgstm--migrationsteps--the-registered-steps-one-per-format-take-any-project-from-format-1-to-the-current-format)

### [MSCMG — MigrationStepChain — one step per format version, chained in order, and a hole in the chain is an error](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-B01 — `Register` keeps the steps sorted by the format they produce, whatever the order they were registered in.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-B02 — `StepsFrom`, asked for the steps from format A to format B, returns the steps producing A+1 through B, in ascending order.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-B03 — A file already at the target format needs no step: the answer is an empty list, not an error.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-B05 — A step may declare code letters renamed by kind of unit, which it does not apply to the YAML files itself (`RenameLetters`, `LetterRename`).](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-B04 — `RenamedKey` reports a key as renamed when any registered step renames it in any file; any other key is not.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-I01 — `AllSteps`, listing the registered steps, hands out a copy: changing the list a caller received never changes the registry.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-X01 — Steps outside the requested interval are never returned: neither those producing the origin or earlier formats, nor those producing formats beyond the target.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-E01 — A step inside the requested interval is missing — the next registered step produces a later format.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

- [MSCMG-E02 — The target is beyond the last registered step.](layers/apoio.md#mscmg--migrationstepchain--one-step-per-format-version-chained-in-order-and-a-hole-in-the-chain-is-an-error)

### [AGRLG — AgentRoles — who is who in a project, and the capabilities each role carries](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B01 — The known roles are dev, qa, reviewer-security, reviewer-performance, reviewer, product-owner and architect, listed in a stable order, each with a title, a sentence of what it does and at least one capability. (`KnownRoles`)](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B02 — Only the product owner and the architect decide the product.](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B03 — The architect decides the structure; the product owner does not.](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B04 — Dev, QA and the reviewers decide neither the product nor the structure, and all of them can review.](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B05 — QA and each reviewer role carry a review lens, all distinct; the dev carries none.](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B06 — A typed role is recognised by its name or a common abbreviation, in English or Portuguese, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; anything else is not recognised. (`ParseRole`)](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-B07 — A role lists its capabilities in alphabetical order, whatever order they were declared in, so the same role always shows them the same way. (`Caps`)](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

- [AGRLG-X01 — An unknown role, including a known name in another case, has no capability at all.](layers/apoio.md#agrlg--agentroles--who-is-who-in-a-project-and-the-capabilities-each-role-carries)

### [USSTS — UserSettings — the agent's local settings: the declared role, kept out of git](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B01 — The settings live in `.anchors/settings.yaml` under the project root. (`Path`)](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B02 — A missing settings file loads as empty settings without error: nothing decided, and escalated cards not handled.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B03 — Without a role, the legacy field has three states: never asked (undecided, not handling escalated cards), declared no (decided, not handling), declared yes (decided, handling).](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B04 — Without a role, a legacy yes grants only the product decision, no other capability.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B05 — A declared role decides the capabilities, winning over the legacy field.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B06 — Saving creates the state folder when missing, and loading gives back what was saved. (`Save`)](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B07 — The saved file opens with a header saying it is local and kept out of git, that only product-owner and architect act on escalated cards, and how to declare the role.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B08 — A typed answer of s, sim, y or yes is yes, and n, nao, não or no is no, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; anything else is no answer. (`ParseAnswer`)](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-B09 — The description of the settings names the role's title and the agent when a role is declared, and points to declaring the role when only the legacy field is set.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

- [USSTS-E01 — The settings file exists but is not valid YAML.](layers/apoio.md#ussts--usersettings--the-agents-local-settings-the-declared-role-kept-out-of-git)

### [TLCNT — TelemetryConfig — the opt-out is easy to find, easy to get right, and the environment overrides the file](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-B01 — `Disabled` answers yes for the words `off`, `0`, `false` and `no` turn telemetry off, whatever their case and with surrounding spaces ignored.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-B02 — With nothing declared in the environment nor in the file, telemetry is on.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-B03 — A non-blank environment value decides alone: `on` in the environment keeps telemetry on over `off` in the file, and `off` in the environment turns it off over `on` in the file.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-B04 — With the environment blank or absent, the file's value decides with the same words.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-I01 — The same value means the same thing in both places: a word that disables through the environment disables through the file, and one that keeps telemetry on does so in both.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

- [TLCNT-X01 — Only the four off-words turn telemetry off; any other text — `on`, `yes`, `disabled`, a typo — leaves it on.](layers/apoio.md#tlcnt--telemetryconfig--the-opt-out-is-easy-to-find-easy-to-get-right-and-the-environment-overrides-the-file)

### [TLEVT — TelemetryEvent — a decision event has a name from a closed vocabulary, a caller-stamped instant and attributes](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

- [TLEVT-B01 — An event created by `New` carries the name and the attributes it was given, unchanged.](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

- [TLEVT-B02 — An event created without attributes carries an empty attribute set, never an absent one.](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

- [TLEVT-B03 — The event's instant is the one returned by the clock the caller passed.](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

- [TLEVT-I01 — The vocabulary is exactly five names, each with its fixed wire value: `claim.served`, `claim.empty`, `check.finished`, `escalate.raised` and `turn.ended`.](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

- [TLEVT-X01 — Does not read the system clock: the instant comes only from the clock passed in.](layers/apoio.md#tlevt--telemetryevent--a-decision-event-has-a-name-from-a-closed-vocabulary-a-caller-stamped-instant-and-attributes)

### [TLNTT — TelemetryNotice — the telemetry notice reaches whoever did not ask for it, once, and says how to turn it off](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-B01 — `Notice`: The first call writes the notice; a later call for the same project root writes nothing, because the first one left its marker.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-B02 — The text states what is sent, what is not sent — naming file content — both ways to turn telemetry off: the `ANCHORS_TELEMETRY=off` environment variable and `telemetry: off` in the configuration — and that it appears once per project on this machine, which is where its marker lives.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-B03 — The marker, recorded by `MarkNoticed`, is written at `.anchors/telemetry-noticed` under the project root, a directory that is kept out of version control, so one person seeing the notice does not silence it for the team.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-B04 — The text comes from the translation catalog, so it is written in the project's language.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-I01 — Showing the notice and asking whether it was shown agree: after a call that wrote the notice, `AlreadyNoticed` answers yes for that root.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-X01 — Does not decide whether telemetry is on: it only announces it; the caller shows it only when telemetry is enabled.](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

- [TLNTT-E01 — The marker cannot be written (the `.anchors` directory cannot be created under the root).](layers/apoio.md#tlntt--telemetrynotice--the-telemetry-notice-reaches-whoever-did-not-ask-for-it-once-and-says-how-to-turn-it-off)

### [TLEMT — TelemetryEmitter — decision events leave as OTLP logs, never block the work, and never carry who uses the product](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B01 — `NewEmitter` with a disabled configuration yields no emitter, and emitting or flushing through the absent emitter does nothing and does not crash.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B02 — A blank endpoint means the default, Honeycomb's logs endpoint.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B03 — Each event is sent as one OTLP log record inside one resource: the record's body is the event name, its time is the event's instant in Unix nanoseconds, and its attributes are the event's attributes.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B04 — Sending happens in the background: emitting returns at once, and a collector that is down neither blocks nor fails the caller.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B05 — Flushing waits for the sends still in flight, so an event emitted just before the process ends reaches the collector.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B06 — Flushing waits at most two seconds, on a deadline of its own that does not depend on the HTTP client's timeout.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B07 — Each request is a POST with a JSON content type and carries the authentication headers of the configuration.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-B08 — With `NoCodes` set, an attribute whose value is a unit's identity code or one of its rule codes (upper-case letters and digits, optionally followed by a rule suffix such as `-B01`) is not sent; every other attribute is. Without it, every attribute is sent.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-I01 — No attribute value leaves as arbitrary content: strings, integers and booleans keep their typed form, and any other value is sent as its type description in parentheses.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-X01 — The resource carries exactly two attributes, the product name `anchors` and its version — never a host, user or repository.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-E01 — REF[TLEMT-B04]: an unreachable collector is the failure B04 answers: the send fails in the background and the caller is never told](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

- [TLEMT-E02 — The collector answers with an error status.](layers/apoio.md#tlemt--telemetryemitter--decision-events-leave-as-otlp-logs-never-block-the-work-and-never-carry-who-uses-the-product)

## comando

### [AGCRG — AgentCards — the cards this agent owns, and the card a pull request declares, read from the tracker](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B01 — With no agent name, no configuration, no workflow block or a workflow with no label, or with no tracker client on the PATH, the agent's card list is empty and no error is raised.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B02 — The tracker is asked for the open cards of the workflow repository carrying the workflow's first label, keeping only those whose last ownership comment names this agent.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B03 — Each card line becomes a card with its number, its title and its state, the state losing the `anchors:` prefix of its label.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B04 — A line that does not have exactly three fields, or whose number is empty, is skipped; the other cards are kept.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B05 — A card with no state label is kept wherever it appears, including as the last line of the answer.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B06 — `FirstLineOfReason`: an issue title made from a reason keeps only the reason's first line, trimmed of surrounding spaces.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B07 — `FirstLineOfReason`: a title longer than 70 characters is cut so that, with a trailing ellipsis, it is exactly 70 characters long; a title of 70 characters or less is kept whole. Characters, not bytes: a multi-byte character is never split, and the title stays valid UTF-8.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B08 — `NumeroDaIssue`: the issue number is the last path segment of an issue URL, trimmed, and only when it is made of digits alone; otherwise the answer is empty.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

- [AGCRG-B09 — `CardDoPR`: the card a pull request declares is the number after the first `Refs`, `Closes`, `Fixes` or `Resolves #N` that starts a line of its body, in any letter case; a keyword in the middle of a line does not count.](layers/comando.md#agcrg--agentcards--the-cards-this-agent-owns-and-the-card-a-pull-request-declares-read-from-the-tracker)

### [CMCLC — CommonCLI — the contract every command shares: how a path becomes a node, how "not governed" is signalled, what the binary says it is](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B01 — The "not governed" error names the path, quoted, says it is not governed, and keeps the path for the caller to read back.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B02 — The exit code that means "not governed" is 3.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B03 — `RelTo`: a path that exists relative to the root is kept as that relative path, cleaned and with forward slashes.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B04 — An absolute path, or a path that does not exist under the root, is resolved from the working directory and expressed relative to the root, with forward slashes.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B05 — `NodeExists`: a node exists only when the map holds a node with exactly that identifier; with no map, no node exists.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B06 — `RelSlug`: a task slug is the path without its last extension only.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B07 — A binary built without a stamp reports the version `dev`, the commit `none` and the date `unknown`.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-B08 — A command that takes files reads each argument as a file or as several separated by commas — the list a `--changed` flag takes —, drops blanks, keeps a file named twice once, and keeps the order; `TakesFiles` gives a command that reading and marks it. (`FileArgs`, `TakesFiles`)](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-I01 — The same file named root-relative or absolute resolves to the same node identifier.](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

- [CMCLC-E01 — The path cannot be expressed relative to the root (the root is relative and the path absolute).](layers/comando.md#cmclc--commoncli--the-contract-every-command-shares-how-a-path-becomes-a-node-how-not-governed-is-signalled-what-the-binary-says-it-is)

### [TLSTT — TelemetrySetup — every command starts telemetry the same way: the opt-outs first, then the notice, then the emitter](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)

- [TLSTT-B01 — A project's `telemetry: off` is read from the project root's configuration, so it holds from the root, from a subdirectory, and with `--root` pointing at the project from elsewhere.](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)

- [TLSTT-B06 — `FlushTelemetry`: waiting for events in flight at exit returns at once when no emitter was built.](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)

- [TLSTT-B07 — When the project configuration does not load, a top-level `telemetry:` line is still read from its text, so a declared `telemetry: off` still builds nothing.](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)

- [TLSTT-B08 — Outside a project — no root found, or a root without the project configuration — no notice is shown, no emitter is built and no mark is written anywhere.](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)

- [TLSTT-X01 — Does not send any event while starting; it only builds the emitter.](layers/comando.md#tlstt--telemetrysetup--every-command-starts-telemetry-the-same-way-the-opt-outs-first-then-the-notice-then-the-emitter)
