### [TSSTT — TaskStatus — discover what the machine knows about the task at hand, so the agent's report does not have to](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B01 — The working tree is read from the root: its branch, and whether it has any uncommitted or untracked change.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B02 — In github mode, a card given by number is read with its labels, and its state is its `anchors:` label — or "closed" when the card is closed, whatever label it kept.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B03 — In github mode without a number, the card is the one the board says this agent owns.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B04 — In github mode, the open cards waiting on a person's decision are listed with their numbers and titles.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B05 — The pull request is the one of the root's branch, looked up from the root; each check counts as running when it has no conclusion or has not completed, as passed when it succeeded, was neutral or was skipped, and as failed otherwise; a legacy commit status that is pending or expected counts as running, and its state is the verdict otherwise.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B06 — The moves the state lock undid on the card are the comments that start with the lock's marker AND were written by the automation's account; each is reduced to its first line, without bold or code marks and without the marker.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B07 — The command prints the report of the state it discovered.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-B08 — The state the turn ended in is recorded as telemetry: the card's state without its prefix, whether there is a pull request, its state, and the counts of checks — never the card's title nor the labels' full names. The attribute names are stable English identifiers (`has_card`, `has_pr`, `clean_tree`, `unpushed`, `card_state`, `pr_state`, `checks_total`, `checks_failed`, `checks_running`), whatever the user's language.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

- [TSSTT-I01 — Each check falls in exactly one class, so the classes add up to the total.](layers/comando.md#tsstt--taskstatus--discover-what-the-machine-knows-about-the-task-at-hand-so-the-agents-report-does-not-have-to)

### [TSRTS — TaskStatusReport — the format of the round's report: where the task is, the verdict, what is missing, and what comes next](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B01 — The sections come in this order: the card, what was undone, the pull request, the working tree, the decisions waiting on a person, the two gaps, and the next step.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B02 — The card line shows its number and its title without the leading `[CODE]`, then what its state means ("under review", "in progress", "closed", …) and its owner when known; without a card it says none was found and to provide `--card N`.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B03 — The undone section appears only when there are reversions: it lists each, says the card moves by fact (the claim delivers, the checks move it to review, the merge moves it to ready-to-test — the merge never closes it, since `pr-body` writes `Refs`), and says how to authorise a deliberate move with the `anchors:manual` label.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B04 — The pull request line says "no check ran" when there are no checks; one class alone reads as count over total; mixed classes are listed one by one, the failed first, then the running, then the passed. Without a pull request it says there is none for the branch.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B05 — The working-tree line shows the branch and says "uncommitted change", the number of unpushed commits, or "up to date with the remote".](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B06 — The waiting section appears only when decisions wait on a person: it lists each number and title without its code, and says no agent resolves these.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B07 — "What I proved" and "What was left out" always appear, as gaps for the agent to fill.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B08 — An uncommitted change comes first, then an unpushed commit, before any other step.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B09 — Without a pull request: a card in progress with a clean, pushed tree is told to open the pull request, with `anchors pr-body` writing the lines that link the card (not closing ones); a card under review or ready for review is told its pull request is on another branch and how to find it; no other card is told to open one.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B10 — With an open pull request: no check → trigger the checks and do not trust a green that does not exist; any running → wait with `--watch` and do not end the turn; any failed → it is work of THIS card, fix it; all passed → the review is missing.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B11 — A closed card is told that `anchors next` asks for the next one; when no step applies, the fallback points to `anchors status` and `anchors next`.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-B12 — The check classes (failed, running, passed) are kept as stable English identifiers and printed in the user's language, through the i18n catalogue.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-I01 — A running check is never reported as passed: a mix of passed and running checks never reads as all of them passing.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

- [TSRTS-X01 — Rendering only formats the state it receives; it looks nothing up.](layers/comando.md#tsrts--taskstatusreport--the-format-of-the-rounds-report-where-the-task-is-the-verdict-what-is-missing-and-what-comes-next)

### [NBLCK — Unblock — open the work card a decision demanded, linked to the card stuck waiting for a person](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B01 — The command takes exactly one card; none or two are refused.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B02 — A blank reason is refused, because whoever takes the new card does not have the context of the decision.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B03 — Outside github mode the command refuses, saying that locally the block is not a label.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B04 — The link label of the blocked card is created on demand before the card is created, and a failure to create it (it already exists) does not stop the command.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B05 — The new card is titled `[unblocks #<n>]` followed by the first line of the reason, and carries the first workflow label, the to-do label and the blocked card's link label.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B06 — The new card's body says which card its delivery unblocks, the reason, where it came from, that the original discussion need not be reopened, and to remove the needs-user mark from the blocked card on delivery; a given file adds a "Where" line, and without it there is none.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B07 — The blocked card receives a comment naming the new card and saying its needs-user mark stays until that delivery.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B08 — The output gives the address of the new card and says the blocked card remains stopped and now says who it waits for.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-B09 — A leading `#` on the card is stripped before it is used.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-I01 — The blocked card keeps its needs-user mark: the command never removes a label from it.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-X01 — The body is handed to the platform through a temporary file, and that file does not survive the command.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-E01 — The platform refuses to create the new card.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

- [NBLCK-E02 — The comment on the blocked card fails after the new card was created.](layers/comando.md#nblck--unblock--open-the-work-card-a-decision-demanded-linked-to-the-card-stuck-waiting-for-a-person)

### [WTCHA — Watch — the background watcher that turns "a file changed" into "there is work in the queue"](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B01 — `status` says "stopped" without a live pid; with one it says running or paused, with the pid, followed by the recorded metadata.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B02 — `start` refuses while a watcher is already running.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B03 — `pause` refuses when no watcher is running, and otherwise leaves the pause flag; `resume` removes it.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B04 — `stop` terminates the running watcher and removes its pid file; stopping a stopped watcher is an error.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B05 — `logs` prints the log as it is, and without a log it fails asking whether the watcher ever ran.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B06 — `run` loads the configuration and the map before looping, and fails naming which one could not be loaded.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B07 — A file created after the start becomes a task, including a file in a folder born after the start; a termination signal ends the loop cleanly, reporting it, and the pid file is removed.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B08 — The whole tree is watched except the directories the ignore list skips, and the first-level files of a new folder are swept once, so those born before the watch took effect are not lost.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B09 — A change in a governed file queues the next piece of its unit's chain, skipping a piece that already exists, and reports the task and the queue's size.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B10 — A piece the unit's layer waives is skipped to the next step of the chain; the layer is the one of the unit's code file, even when the change is in a derived piece.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B11 — A file outside the structure, a file already gone, a file the project's ignore list covers and an editor's temporary queue nothing.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B12 — A delivery record at the root of `changes/` for a plan queues the review of the whole plan; for a unit it queues the review only once the unit has code and a test, and otherwise says the review waits for the unit to close; a record under `changes/reviewed/` queues nothing.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B13 — A unit whose layer waives the test is reviewed as soon as its code exists, a test beside the code in any supported language closes the unit, and a record with no readable unit does not hold the review.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B14 — A delivery record is any `.md` directly under `changes/`; one without a unit line is still a delivery.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B15 — A task's id is the path's slug, the step and a short hash: the same path and step give the same id, another step another id, and no id holds a `/`.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-B16 — A governed file the map does not have enters it the moment the watcher sees it — read alone, with its unit —, and the watcher's copy of the map is reloaded; without a map on disk, nothing is written.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-I01 — A task still in the queue is never queued twice: the same change again is reported as already in the queue.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-I02 — Every change is handled by the loop itself, one at a time — the debounce timer only hands the path back to it. A change still inside its debounce window when the loop ends is handled before the loop returns, and nothing is handled after it.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-X01 — Handling a change only queues: it writes nothing outside the task queue.](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

- [WTCHA-E01 — REF[WTCHA-B06]: the configuration or the map cannot be loaded, and B06 fails `run` naming which](layers/comando.md#wtcha--watch--the-background-watcher-that-turns-a-file-changed-into-there-is-work-in-the-queue)

### [WTDMW — WatchDaemon — the watcher started in the background survives the terminal that started it](layers/comando.md#wtdmw--watchdaemon--the-watcher-started-in-the-background-survives-the-terminal-that-started-it)

- [WTDMW-B01 — On a unix-like system, a detached child leads its own process group, distinct from the parent's.](layers/comando.md#wtdmw--watchdaemon--the-watcher-started-in-the-background-survives-the-terminal-that-started-it)

- [WTDMW-B02 — On Windows, a detached child is created in a new process group, so the console's Ctrl+C sent to the parent's group does not reach it.](layers/comando.md#wtdmw--watchdaemon--the-watcher-started-in-the-background-survives-the-terminal-that-started-it)

- [WTDMW-I01 — Exactly one detachment implementation is built for any target platform.](layers/comando.md#wtdmw--watchdaemon--the-watcher-started-in-the-background-survives-the-terminal-that-started-it)

- [WTDMW-X01 — Detaching does not start the child.](layers/comando.md#wtdmw--watchdaemon--the-watcher-started-in-the-background-survives-the-terminal-that-started-it)

### [WRPRW — WorkPrompt — compose the work prompt of one stage over one target, from what the project declares](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B01 — The command refuses an artifact outside the stages it composes, a missing `--for`, and a project whose configuration does not load.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B02 — A target in a spec, feature or test layer is redirected to its unit — the file the map says that spec specifies (also through the spec a feature or test is linked to), else the code file with the same stem beside it — with a note on standard error; a code file is not redirected, and a piece whose unit does not exist is not redirected.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B03 — When the target's layer waives the stage's piece, the prompt is only a STOP saying the layer waives it and not to create it.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B04 — When the target's layer is declarative and the stage is spec, feature or test, the prompt is only a STOP saying the layer is recognized and has no piece of its own.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B05 — The heading names the stage and the target — "Work: <artifact> of", "Review of", or "WHOLE review —" — and the role follows: producer, reviewer of the unit, or reviewer of the whole.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B06 — The target section names the file, its layer with its regime and its tags, or says the layer is unclassified and to confirm it.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B07 — "Read first" lists the artifact's guide, then every project guide that governs the artifact or one of the layer's tags, each once and sorted, then the target and its neighbours; without such guides it says no project guide governs the layer.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B08 — The pieces are listed at the paths the project derives for the target's layer — the stage's own piece marked, the existing ones (under the project root) marked, overridden paths noted, waived pieces marked not to be created — with the unit's name cut at its compound suffix; without derived paths it says so, and a declarative layer's code stage lists only the file itself.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B09 — The feature and test stages list the project's regime tags, sorted, with the surface each is proved on.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B10 — Each stage states what is NOT its scope.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B11 — Each stage has its procedure; a declarative layer gets the declarative procedure, and the layer's own extra steps for the stage are appended.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B12 — "What the gates will demand" lists, once per check, the gates that apply to the stage (the test stage also owes the feature-test match), marks informative ones, and omits gates it has no description for.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B13 — A review confronts the pieces that exist and the pending delivery records of the unit, sorted; without one it says the record is in the card's comments in github mode, and that there is no record otherwise.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B14 — The open findings recorded for the unit (to do and in progress) are listed before writing: an issue counts when one of the paths in its name is a piece of the unit — the unit's stem followed by the piece's suffix — so a unit whose name only contains the stem (`src/pricing-v2.ts`, `lib/src/pricing.ts`) is another unit.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B15 — The test stage and the unit review explain the execution signals: ingesting the suite's report and the unit's mutation report.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B16 — Producing stages end with how to record the delivery with `anchors deliver`; reviews end with how to close the review with `anchors judge`, including findings in another unit.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B17 — The verification runs the checks over the piece this stage produces — not over a code file that may not exist yet — first without recording, then once more recording.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B18 — The legitimate waivers are listed for the stage: `@no-mark` and `@no-scenario` for a spec, `@no-paginate` and `@allow-boundary` for code.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B19 — When the ruler does not decide, the spec stage is told to write the question in the spec's open-decisions section, or its "none" value; the other stages are told to read that section.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-B20 — The code stage requires marking each rule in the code when the project's rule-marking policy is required, and only suggests it otherwise.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-I01 — A prompt never both records a delivery and closes a review.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-X01 — Composing the prompt writes nothing to the project.](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-X02 — Wherever the prompt cites the open-decisions section it uses one title and one "none" value, the catalogue's; and it cites configuration keys and checks by their current names (`optional_unit_edges`, `rule-implemented`, `tests-pass`).](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

- [WRPRW-E01 — REF[WRPRW-B01]: an unknown artifact, a missing target or an unloadable configuration, which B01 refuses before composing anything](layers/comando.md#wrprw--workprompt--compose-the-work-prompt-of-one-stage-over-one-target-from-what-the-project-declares)

### [DTAUI — Audit — the dossier of everything pending on one file, for fixing it in one pass](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B01 — A target the map does not know is refused with "file … is not in the map", and nothing is audited.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B02 — Without `--impact` the scope is the target alone, and the header reads "audit: <target> — the file".](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B03 — With `--impact` the scope adds the nodes the target propagates to and the nodes that validate it, and the header reads "the unit (N nodes on the impact path)".](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B04 — A gate that passed or was skipped is dropped. A failing gate is marked ✗, a pending one ~ and one awaiting judgment ⏳, each with only the first line of its detail.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B05 — A doctor finding is shown only when its subject is in the scope, marked ⚠ for a warning and ℹ for information.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B06 — Only a failing gate and a warning finding count toward "N actionable pending item(s)"; pending, judgment and informational lines are shown but not counted.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B07 — When nothing is left to show, the dossier says "✓ nothing pending".](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B08 — The target's block prints first, marked ●; every other node in scope prints after it, marked ○ and "(impact)".](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-B09 — The impact nodes print sorted by path, so the same tree gives the same dossier on every run.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-I01 — Nothing about a node outside the audited scope reaches the dossier: neither a gate line nor a doctor finding.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-E01 — The root has no loadable configuration.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-E02 — The root has no loadable map.](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

- [DTAUI-E03 — REF[DTAUI-B01]: a target outside the map is the failure B01 answers: the command refuses it by name](layers/comando.md#dtaui--audit--the-dossier-of-everything-pending-on-one-file-for-fixing-it-in-one-pass)

### [CMPLN — Compliance — the state of each regulatory duty, grouped by the norm that imposes it](layers/comando.md#cmpln--compliance--the-state-of-each-regulatory-duty-grouped-by-the-norm-that-imposes-it)

- [CMPLN-B01 — Each duty is printed under its norm: a pack duty under the pack's authority, or the pack's name when it declares none; an inline obligation under "declared in the project". Norms and the duties inside each norm are sorted by name.](layers/comando.md#cmpln--compliance--the-state-of-each-regulatory-duty-grouped-by-the-norm-that-imposes-it)

- [CMPLN-B02 — Each duty line is marked · when no node is subject, ✗ when fewer subjects comply than are subject, and ✓ otherwise. It shows the subject and complying counts, the pack article when there is one, and appends the assumed debts and the waivers when there are any.](layers/comando.md#cmpln--compliance--the-state-of-each-regulatory-duty-grouped-by-the-norm-that-imposes-it)

- [CMPLN-B03 — A duty with subjects, none complying and no declared debt gets a "⚠ NONE complies" line naming its targets, warning that a disconnected target looks like total violation, and naming where the target is declared: `pack_values:` for a pack duty, the obligation's `must_appear_in:` for an inline one. A duty whose only gap is declared debt does not warn.](layers/comando.md#cmpln--compliance--the-state-of-each-regulatory-duty-grouped-by-the-norm-that-imposes-it)

- [CMPLN-B04 — With `--verbose`, each duty lists the nodes that do not comply. Without it, when some duty has a gap, the report ends with the hint "(use --verbose …)".](layers/comando.md#cmpln--compliance--the-state-of-each-regulatory-duty-grouped-by-the-norm-that-imposes-it)

- [FLWOX-B08 — The mermaid drawing turns step codes into valid identifiers, replaces double quotes in labels, puts the fitted action on a second line with a native line break, draws terminals in the stadium shape, labels each exit with the short name of its result (or its condition), and highlights the entry and the terminals.](layers/comando.md#flwox--flow--build-draw-and-navigate-the-work-flows-kept-in-the-map)

- [FLWOX-B09 — The mermaid direction accepts top-down, left-right, right-left and bottom-top in any case; any other value falls back to top-down.](layers/comando.md#flwox--flow--build-draw-and-navigate-the-work-flows-kept-in-the-map)

- [FLWOX-I01 — What the build writes into the map is what drawing and navigating read: the drawing is derived from the stored graph, never from a stored picture.](layers/comando.md#flwox--flow--build-draw-and-navigate-the-work-flows-kept-in-the-map)

### [MPCTI — Impact — what a change to one file reaches, in both directions of the map](layers/comando.md#mpcti--impact--what-a-change-to-one-file-reaches-in-both-directions-of-the-map)

- [MPCTI-B01 — For a spec, the propagate direction lists the artifacts that depend on it: the code and the test it specifies.](layers/comando.md#mpcti--impact--what-a-change-to-one-file-reaches-in-both-directions-of-the-map)

### [NGSTI — Ingest — binds the test and log signals the project produced to the nodes of the map](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B01 — In one pass of `IngestArtifacts` (the entry the ingest command and the test commands share), the execution report reaches the test node (passed, failed and skipped counts), the passing case codes are proven on the spec that declares them, and the coverage and mutation reports reach the code node.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B03 — When the project declares its code length, the case names of the execution report are read with it, so a rule code of that length is proven by its passing case.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B04 — An ingestion not run by the test commands warns on the error stream and proceeds, by default.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B05 — An ingestion run by the test commands never complains, even when the project refuses manual ingestion.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B06 — A project with no test or mutation suite declared, or with no configuration at all, is not asked to use the test commands.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B07 — The suite key is the report's path from the project root; a report outside the repository is keyed by the external prefix and its file name, the same on every machine.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B08 — A full run of a suite inside the repository drops from the map the suites ingested from outside it, and says so.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B09 — A partial run, or another report from outside the repository, drops no external suite.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B10 — When two paths of one report name the same node, the path equal to the node id wins, whatever order the report lists them in.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B11 — A line coverage entry for a file changed after the report was written is marked as predating the file; a file older than the report, or one not on disk, is not.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B12 — Log ingestion binds each occurrence of a declared failure code to the spec that declares it, with the number of occurrences, stamped with the spec's current revision.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B13 — Log ingestion reports the failure codes found in the logs that no spec declares.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B14 — A test file's run time in the report is the sum of its cases' times, kept in the map under the report's suite.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B16 — An ingestion that follows a run of `anchors test` or `anchors mutation` first takes the revs of the tree as it is now, so a proof of a spec edited after the last `map build` stays fresh once the map is rebuilt; a manual ingestion keeps the map's revs, since its report may be older than the tree.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B17 — An ingestion that follows a run first adds to the map the governed files it does not have yet — read alone, with their units —, so the proof of a spec created after the last `map build` reaches it.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B18 — A whole-run coverage report a declared test suite names in its `lcov:` marks as omitted every code file the suite covers and the report left out, and says how many; a partial run, or a report no suite declares, marks nothing. (`suiteOfLcov`)](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B20 — A file a targeted mutation run handed to the tool (`MutationTargets`) that its report does not list is recorded as measured at its revision with no mutant, so `mutation-score` answers "nothing to mutate".](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B19 — A JUnit case with no `file` finds its test file from its class and name: the class names a test folder of the map by path suffix (segments split by `/`, or by `.` when it has none, dropped from the front until one exists; the root's folder when none does), and the case's file is the one test file there whose dialect `definition` defines the case's top-level test, the name before `/`; no folder, no file, or two files give the case no file. (`caseFileResolver`)](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-B15 — A report's signals are kept under its path relative to the root; a report outside the repository is kept under `external/` and its file name. (`SuiteKey`)](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-I01 — Ingesting the logs replaces the occurrences bound before on every spec: the same logs ingested twice leave the same counts.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-X01 — A failure code no spec declares is bound to no node of the map.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-E01 — No report and no log option is given.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-E02 — A manual ingestion in a project that declares manual ingestion must be refused.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-E03 — Log ingestion in a project that declares no log paths.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-E04 — A report that is missing or cannot be parsed.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

- [NGSTI-E05 — The map cannot be loaded while ingesting reports.](layers/comando.md#ngsti--ingest--binds-the-test-and-log-signals-the-project-produced-to-the-nodes-of-the-map)

### [JDGUE — Judge — records an AI's verdict on a judgment gate with the same bookkeeping as a deterministic gate](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B01 — The verdict is read case-insensitively, and the legacy spelling of the waiver is a waiver from validation to the stamp and the printed word.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B02 — A pass needs no reason; a fail and a waiver must name one (`ValidateVerdict` refuses them otherwise).](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B03 — The gate must be a declared judgment gate matched by its exact name; the cycle's `review` is accepted without being declared.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B04 — A gate that declares a guide is stamped on the edge from the guide to the target, with `ok` for pass, `issue` for fail and `waived` for waiver, and the judgment counts as answered for that gate.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B05 — A gate with no guide edge to the target is stamped on every edge of the target, with the gate's name.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B06 — A target not in the map is recorded on the piece of the same unit that is in the map, and the output says which.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B12 — The piece of the same unit is found by name from a code or a test target: the test suffixes (`.test`, `.spec`, `_test`) are dropped, and the candidates are the spec, the feature, and the Go and TypeScript code and test names, plus the target's own extension.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B07 — A fail opens an issue whose body is the report; the same report again changes nothing, and a different report reopens the issue and appends it.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B08 — A pass resolves the open issue of that gate and target; a waiver resolves it too, announcing a waiver and never a pass.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B09 — In manual workflow mode the verdict is stamped and the report printed, but no issue is written unless recording issues is asked; in every other mode the issue is written.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B10 — A fail with a patch opens a fix suggestion named after the gate and the target, carrying the patch.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-B11 — Recording a verdict closes the queue's judge task for that gate and target; the pending switch lists the queued judge tasks — those of the judgment kind, and those with the legacy judge verb — or says none is waiting.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-I01 — The stamp always tells the three verdicts apart: a waiver is never stamped `ok`, whatever spelling it came in.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-X01 — Does not announce a waiver as a pass, in any output.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E01 — No target is given and the pending switch is off.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E02 — No gate is given.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E03 — The verdict is none of the three.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E04 — REF[JDGUE-B02]: a fail or a waiver without a reason is the refusal B02 states](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E05 — The gate is not a declared judgment gate.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E06 — There is no map.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

- [JDGUE-E07 — The target is not in the map and no piece of its unit is.](layers/comando.md#jdgue--judge--records-an-ais-verdict-on-a-judgment-gate-with-the-same-bookkeeping-as-a-deterministic-gate)

### [MPCMM — MapCommand — builds the dependency map from the project and answers questions about it](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B01 — A rebuild keeps the judgment stamps the previous map carried on the edges that still exist.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B02 — A rebuild keeps the flow graph of the previous map, which the build itself does not produce.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B03 — When a gate has fewer judgment stamps than in the previous map, the build warns naming the gate and the count before and after; with no loss, or with a gain, it says nothing.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B04 — The edge summary lists the unit's edge types first, in a fixed order, then every other type alphabetically, so no type is hidden; with no edges there is no summary.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B05 — When the layer of a file was decided by pattern length, the build warns once per pair of winning and losing layers, with the number of files and one example, and says what the wrong choice costs; with no such file it says nothing.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B11 — A file whose layer is decided by a declared priority is not reported as a guess: once one of the matching layers declares a priority, the build no longer warns about that file.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B06 — Showing a file lists the edges that reach it and the edges that leave it, marking a file with nothing above it as a top and one with nothing below as a leaf.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B07 — The orphans switch lists the nodes with no edge at all, with their kind and count.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B08 — The statistics switch gives the node and edge totals, the nodes by kind and the edges by type, each in a fixed order.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B09 — The worklist lists every node in topological order, the ruler before what it governs and the spec before its code, with the node count.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-B10 — The worklist with the pending switch runs the gates and lists only the nodes with a failing gate; a judgment that is only pending does not count.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-X01 — The stamp-loss and layer-ambiguity warnings never fail the build.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-E01 — `build` finds no configuration file.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

- [MPCMM-E02 — `show` finds no map file.](layers/comando.md#mpcmm--mapcommand--builds-the-dependency-map-from-the-project-and-answers-questions-about-it)

### [MPMRM — MapMerge — the git merge driver that unites two versions of the map instead of merging text](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B01 — The result is written onto our side's file, which is what git expects of a merge driver.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B02 — A node that exists only on the other side is added to the result, and a node only on our side stays.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B03 — A node both sides have keeps our side's version: its revision is not reconciled here, because only a rebuild over the merged tree knows the file's content. What was ingested on it is joined instead (B08).](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B04 — An edge that exists only on the other side is added to the result with the judgments it carries; an edge is identified by its type and its two ends.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B05 — When only one side has judged an edge both sides share, that side's judgments are in the result, whichever side it is: a side with no judgment on the edge never erases the other's.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B07 — On an edge both sides share, judgments are joined by gate: a gate only one side judged is kept, and a gate both sides judged keeps the judgment with the latest change date, ours on a tie; the edge's check stamp follows the same rule.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B08 — A node both sides have gets the other side's observed failures joined by rule (the latest last occurrence wins, ours on a tie), and the other side's test signal — and its declarations of kept evidence, when ours has none — when both carry the same revision; the flow graph is the union of both sides' states, by code, and transitions.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

- [MPMRM-B06 — After writing, the error stream reports how many judgments the result keeps and, when there are more than our side had, how many came from the other side.](layers/comando.md#mpmrm--mapmerge--the-git-merge-driver-that-unites-two-versions-of-the-map-instead-of-merging-text)

(`codeShapeRE`)](layers/comando.md#cdcmc--codecommand--a-new-unit-gets-an-identity-code-that-no-other-unit-in-the-map-already-owns-and-the-codes-in-use-are-listed-from-the-map)

### [CMMSC — CommitMsg — the commit subject is confronted with the format the changelog will read, before the commit exists](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B01 — The subject is the first line of the file that is neither blank nor a `#` comment, trimmed.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B02 — A subject git generates (starting with `Merge `, `Revert `, `fixup! `, `squash! ` or `Reapply `) passes; a human subject merely starting alike does not escape.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B03 — A subject of the form `type: text`, `type(scope): text`, with an optional `!` before the colon, passes when the type is known.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B04 — The type must be lowercase and one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert; anything else is refused naming the type.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B05 — An empty scope, `type():`, is refused.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B06 — A subject longer than the limit of 100 characters (see `CMMSC-B14`) is refused, and the diagnosis says the detail belongs in the body; a subject of exactly the limit passes.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B07 — A subject whose text ends in a period is refused.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B08 — Each defect has its own diagnosis, distinct from every other.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B09 — A capital letter at the start of the subject text is allowed.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B10 — A rejection repeats the subject, teaches the `type(scope): what changed` format with examples, and lists the accepted types.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B11 — A message with no subject (empty, or only comments) passes.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B12 — The checks run in order (format, lowercase type, known type, non-empty scope, non-empty text, a space after the colon, length, final period) and only the first defect is reported.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B13 — A known type followed by nothing after the colon is refused.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B14 — The subject limit counts characters, not bytes: a subject of 100 accented letters passes, and the diagnosis of a longer one gives its length in characters.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B15 — A subject with no space after the colon (`feat:x`) is refused with its own diagnosis, as commitlint refuses it.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-B16 — A `Bug:` footer — in the trailing paragraphs made only of `Key: value` lines, so a `Co-Authored-By:` block after it does not hide it — marks a fix of a defect that shipped: it is refused when empty, when spelled other than `Bug:`, or on a commit that is not a `fix`; a message without it, or with a body paragraph of prose starting with "Bug:", passes.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-I01 — REF[CMMSC-B03]: every subject commitlint accepts in the confronted cases, except the empty scope, passes here — the ruler never diverges to the looser side](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-X01 — The command does not refuse an empty message and does not rewrite the message: it only accepts or refuses.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [CMMSC-E01 — The message file cannot be read.](layers/comando.md#cmmsc--commitmsg--the-commit-subject-is-confronted-with-the-format-the-changelog-will-read-before-the-commit-exists)

- [DCCMD-X01 — `docs build` never writes the map: the rebuilt map lives only for the compilation.](layers/comando.md#dccmd--docscommand--the-documentation-is-compiled-from-the-specs-through-templates-against-a-map-rebuilt-from-the-tree)

### [FRZEX — Freeze — the project is stopped in three layers with a written reason, and thawed by undoing exactly those layers](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B05 — In github mode with a repository, the freeze creates the `anchors-freeze` rule on the remote and opens an issue with a fixed title, reporting its link; in any other mode it calls nothing on the remote.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B06 — With `--no-ruleset`, the remote rule is not created and the issue is still opened.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B07 — Freezing a project already frozen changes nothing and shows the existing reason.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B08 — A remote layer that fails (push, rule or issue) is a warning naming it, and the command still succeeds with the local file frozen; the thaw warns the same way.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B09 — The thaw removes the freeze lines, commits and pushes `chore(anchors): thaw`, deletes the rule found by its name and closes the issue found by its exact title.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B10 — Thawing a project that is not frozen changes nothing and says so.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B11 — When the remote has no freeze rule and no open freeze issue, the thaw deletes and closes nothing, without error.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B12 — The deprecated Portuguese flag names (`--motivo`, `--sem-ruleset`, `--sem-push`) still drive the commands.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-B13 — A configuration that already declares a top-level `enabled:` or `freeze_reason:` (with any indented continuation lines) has those lines replaced, not stacked on: the frozen file holds exactly one of each key and still loads, frozen, with the new reason; the thaw then removes them and the project loads enabled.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-I01 — A freeze followed by a thaw gives back the configuration byte for byte, when it declared no top-level `enabled:` or `freeze_reason:` of its own (otherwise see `FRZEX-B13`).](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-X01 — The configuration is never reserialized: the freeze only adds its two lines (after removing any top-level `enabled:`/`freeze_reason:` already there) and the thaw only removes top-level lines with those keys.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-E01 — `anchors.yaml` is missing or does not load, for freeze or thaw.](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

- [FRZEX-E02 — REF[FRZEX-B08]: a failing remote layer is the failure this command handles, by warning and keeping the local brake](layers/comando.md#frzex--freeze--the-project-is-stopped-in-three-layers-with-a-written-reason-and-thawed-by-undoing-exactly-those-layers)

### [ININT — InitNonInteractive — the init that an agent answers with flags: it asks in JSON, and writes only a complete, valid set of answers](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B01 — With no answer and no `--defaults`, the command prints the questions as JSON with `escrito: false`, whether the DISCOVER phase is needed, and how to answer, and writes nothing.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B02 — The given answers reach the configuration: the chosen artifact layers, co-location, the default gates, the manual workflow, and the header guide in `guides/` when no guide directory was detected.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B05 — One refused answer refuses the whole set: the command prints JSON with `escrito: false`, every answer's status and the error, fails, and writes nothing.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B06 — `--defaults` with no other answer writes the configuration from the inferred defaults.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B08 — `--layers` keeps only the chosen code layers and prunes the others; without it, no layer is pruned.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B09 — The success JSON has `escrito: true`, the written file, the answers' status and the next step: the DISCOVER phase when the project needs it, otherwise `anchors map build`.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B10 — Each `--governs GUIDE=tag1,tag2` rule is written to the configuration as one governs rule per non-blank tag, guides in sorted order.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B11 — With the contributing answer yes (the default), a project with no `CONTRIBUTING.md` gets one rendered from the written configuration, and the success JSON says it was written; an existing one stays byte for byte, and the success JSON carries the section that would be added. `--contributing=false` touches nothing.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-B12 — When the default gates are seeded, the success JSON carries `gate_scripts`: a gate step doing more than calling one tool is written in the project's language, with the family's example; with no gates seeded it carries none.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-I01 — Either every answer is accepted and the file is written, or nothing is written.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-X01 — The non-interactive mode never prompts: every exchange is JSON on standard output.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-E01 — A `--governs` rule has no `=`.](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [ININT-E02 — REF[ININT-B05]: a refused answer is the failure this mode handles, by refusing the set and writing nothing](layers/comando.md#inint--initnoninteractive--the-init-that-an-agent-answers-with-flags-it-asks-in-json-and-writes-only-a-complete-valid-set-of-answers)

- [MGCMM-B12 — When the project crosses format 7, a file other than the spec that carries, as its own `code:`, the code its unit's spec owns has that line turned into `ref: <code>` with a code of its own above it.](layers/comando.md#mgcmm--migratecommand--the-command-the-format-error-promises-bringing-the-map-and-the-config-up-to-this-binarys-format)

- [MGCMM-X01 — The command does not know which keys each format renamed: the steps belong to the migration package, and this unit only applies them and reports.](layers/comando.md#mgcmm--migratecommand--the-command-the-format-error-promises-bringing-the-map-and-the-config-up-to-this-binarys-format)

- [NWTMN-B01 — The catalog holds seven kinds — action, feature, flow, plan, product, spec, test — and `new` gives birth to each at the given path with the given identity.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B06 — The test body is written in the idiom of each known family (a Python test function, a Go test function, a JUnit test, an xUnit fact, a Rust test, an RSpec block, a PHPUnit method, or a describe/it block), with no other language's syntax.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B08 — For a family it does not know, the test body is an instruction to write a case with the scenario code in its name, not a guessed syntax.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B09 — The twelve spec presets (api, backend-logic, component, handler, hook, mobile-logic, repository, schema, screen, service, store, validation) are each an ordered set of catalog sections, opening with the title and closing with the open decisions.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B10 — Product doctrine has sections of its own, emits `-R` rules, and its header declares no layer.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B11 — The Python and Rust test functions are named by the snake_case of the unit name: each run of separators (`-`, space, `.`, `_`) becomes one `_`, an uppercase letter starts a new word only after a lowercase letter or a digit or when it opens a word after an acronym, and there is no leading or trailing `_` (`My-Name` → `my_name`, `HTTPServer` → `http_server`).](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-B12 — The spec catalog ties rules to what they use: `validations` realizes `V`, `presentation-validations` realizes `P`, and `rule-uses` realizes no letter; each emits a table whose first column is the rule's code and whose second is what it uses; `rule-uses` is in every preset, `validations` in the screen and validation presets, `presentation-validations` in the screen and component ones.](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-I01 — REF[NWTMN-B05]: the letters the catalog emits and the letters the engine reads are the same set](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

- [NWTMN-X01 — REF[NWTMN-B08]: the catalog never guesses the syntax of a language it does not know](layers/comando.md#nwtmn--newtemplates--the-catalog-of-artifact-skeletons-which-kinds-exist-their-headers-their-sections-and-the-presets-that-pick-them)

### [SYCMS — SynthesizeCommand — two pull requests in content conflict become one card that asks for the best of each, and every end points at it](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B03 — The card's body cites both pull requests with their origin cards and titles, lists the conflicting files, asks for the best of each, and warns against discarding a side without saying why.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B04 — With one side only, the body cites no empty pull request, says the other side was not identified, points at the file's history to find it, and gives the instructions in the singular.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B05 — The card is labelled with the project's first workflow label, `anchors:to-do`, and an `under-<card>` label for each origin card.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B06 — Each pull request is commented with where the work continued (the other pull request, or the integration branch when there is none) and closed; each origin card is commented with the new card's link.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B07 — A comment or a close that fails is a warning on standard error naming it, and the command still succeeds.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B08 — The closing line names only the pull requests actually closed, one or many, and lists a pull request whose close failed as still open.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B09 — `--dry-run` prints the title and the body, and creates, comments on and closes nothing.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-B10 — The title, the body and the comments come in the project's language.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-I01 — No pull request is closed unless the synthesis card exists.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-X01 — The card never picks a side and the command never merges or resolves the conflict.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

- [SYCMS-E01 — The card cannot be opened on the host.](layers/comando.md#sycms--synthesizecommand--two-pull-requests-in-content-conflict-become-one-card-that-asks-for-the-best-of-each-and-every-end-points-at-it)

### [BDGRN — BudgetRun — run a suite's files fastest first until a time budget is spent](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B01 — The plan is the suite's timed files, fastest first with ties by path, then the files no suite has timed, by path; a file only other suites timed, a support file, and a file of another kind are left out.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B02 — A batch takes, from the front of the plan, the timed files whose times fit in what remains; when even the fastest does not fit, nothing more runs. After the timed files, the untimed ones run one per batch.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B03 — A batch still running at the deadline is stopped with its whole process group — first a TERM, so a tool that works in place can restore the source, then a KILL of whatever is left after a grace of 10 seconds — and nothing of it is ingested. On Windows, which has no TERM to trap, the process is killed at once.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B04 — Each batch runs through `run_changed:` with its files and is ingested as a partial run; the end reports how many files ran, how many were left, and whether the deadline cut a batch.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B05 — A mutation budget runs one file per batch, and records in the map, under the suite, how long that file's run took.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B06 — A batch that fails does not stop the budget: the next batches run, and the command fails at the end naming the suites with a failed batch.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B07 — A suite with no `run_changed:` or no report, or a budget together with `--changed`, is refused before anything runs.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-B08 — The plan holds only the files the suite's `paths:` cover.](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-E01 — REF[BDGRN-B07]: a suite the budget cannot run in batches](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

- [BDGRN-E02 — The map cannot be loaded](layers/comando.md#bdgrn--budgetrun--run-a-suites-files-fastest-first-until-a-time-budget-is-spent)

### [CGPCH — CheckGatePipeline — confronts the map's nodes against the declared gates, records the verdicts and reports the profile](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B01 — With the full-sweep flag, every node of the map is confronted, and the header names the scope, the number of nodes and of gates.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B02 — With changed files, the check confronts the union of their impact paths — each file, what propagates from it and what validates it — and no node off those paths.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B03 — The tests whose contract stamps point at a changed file enter that file's impact path; tests with no stamp on it do not.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B70 — The other pieces of a changed file's unit enter its impact path by name, whether or not the map links them: spec, feature, code and test, the test named with the Go suffix or the TypeScript one, and the code with the changed file's own extension.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B04 — Changed paths are compared in the map's form: relative to the root, cleaned, with forward slashes, whether the caller passed them absolute or relative.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B05 — A changed file is not governed when it matches no layer, or when it lies under a directory the scan ignores, such as the issues folder that holds the Anchors record.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B06 — In a batch of changed files, the not-governed ones are dropped and the rest confronted; when every file is not governed, the answer is not-governed, naming the first file and counting the others.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B67 — A plan's progress companion is not governed, while the plan beside it stays governed.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

- [CGPCH-B07 — Only the gates of the requested phase and category are charged; when none is left, the check says so and runs nothing.](layers/comando.md#cgpch--checkgatepipeline--confronts-the-maps-nodes-against-the-declared-gates-records-the-verdicts-and-reports-the-profile)

### [KPEVD — KeepEvidence — a change that proves nothing new keeps the files' evidence](layers/comando.md#kpevd--keepevidence--a-change-that-proves-nothing-new-keeps-the-files-evidence)
