- [KPEVD-B03 — A file whose evidence is already at its content, or that has none, is said to have nothing to keep, and is left as it was.](layers/comando.md#kpevd--keepevidence--a-change-that-proves-nothing-new-keeps-the-files-evidence)

- [KPEVD-B04 — The `@contract` stamps of the doubles pointing at the files kept are refreshed and listed, under the same declaration.](layers/comando.md#kpevd--keepevidence--a-change-that-proves-nothing-new-keeps-the-files-evidence)

- [KPEVD-B05 — When the file's signal lacks suites the map at HEAD holds for it — the rebuild dropped the signal and only some suites ran again at the new content —, those suites come back from HEAD and are carried with the rest; a suite run again keeps its new measurement. A suite that ran again and proved nothing here also comes back: the command is the author's declaration that the change proves nothing new.](layers/comando.md#kpevd--keepevidence--a-change-that-proves-nothing-new-keeps-the-files-evidence)

- [RPRTS-B11 — The issues perspective counts issues per state, then lists the open issues waiting on the user, the open agent work and the deferred ones, each list only when not empty, then the live tasks or an empty queue.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-B12 — The inconsistencies perspective lists every health finding grouped by check, the failures of the quality gates, and the total.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-B13 — A finding section takes the findings whose check starts with its name, titles itself with their count, caps the list at 25 saying how many are left, and is absent when there is none.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-B14 — Without anchors.yaml the perspectives say what is missing instead of inventing: the quality one that no gate is declared, the configuration one that the file was not found, the issues one its zero counts and empty queue, and the structure and inconsistencies ones that the health validator needs the file; the all form still writes every perspective.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-I01 — An issue waiting on the user is listed only as the user's, never also as agent work.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-X01 — Generating the reports leaves the map as it was: they write only the report files.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-E01 — The map does not exist or cannot be read, for a single perspective or for all.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

- [RPRTS-E02 — The destination cannot be created or written.](layers/comando.md#rprts--reports--markdown-perspectives-on-what-anchors-already-measures-written-into-docs)

### [SLCTN — RunSelection — a run takes only what is stale and below the minimum, unless told otherwise](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B01 — A file is placed by two answers — fresh or stale, passing or below the minimum — into one of four boxes; a file with no result is never measured.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B02 — By default a run takes the files stale and below the minimum and the ones never measured; `--include-fresh` adds the fresh ones below the minimum, `--include-passing` the stale passing ones, both together the fresh passing ones too, and `--skip-unmeasured` leaves out the never measured.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B03 — A test file is stale when it or anything it exercises changed since its result; its passing is read from the suite's own layer when the file ran in several; a file whose cases were all skipped is not passing.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B04 — A code file's mutation result is stale when measured at another revision of the file — its own, not the one a later coverage ingestion moves —, and one taken under load — more timed-out mutants than the gate's ceiling — counts as stale; it passes at the report's floor or 70% when the report declares none, and a file where no mutant ran passes.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B05 — A test file belongs to the suite that timed it; before any time, to the suite whose layer ran it; a file no suite ran is offered to every suite.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B06 — Support files and targets the matching gate declares in `no_signal` are never run.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B07 — The run says how many files it selected and, by state, how many it left out and the flag that would take them.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B08 — A suite with no `run_changed:` runs whole, saying it cannot run a subset; with a budget it is refused before anything runs.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B09 — When the selection takes no file, the suite says so and runs nothing.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B10 — The selected files run in as few batches as the command-line ceiling allows, each ingested as a partial run; a file longer than the ceiling still runs alone.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B11 — `--all` runs the suites whole through `run:`; it is refused with `--changed` or with a state flag, and the state flags are refused with `--changed`.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B12 — A suite that declares `paths:` is handed only the files they cover, test and code files alike; the files outside them are neither run nor counted as left out.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B13 — A file the matching gate does not confront — outside its `on:` kinds, carrying one of its `exclude_tags`, lacking all of its `tags` — is never run for it; a gate entry that declares no kinds filters nothing.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B14 — A test run also takes the test files of the rules a contract field changed since the last commit reaches, when the suite runs them — saying which were added and why —, whatever state their own file is in.](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-B15 — The map is read as a build would leave it now: a file edited since the last build has no result — the build drops the result of another version — and is selected as never measured; an unchanged file keeps its result. (`currentRevs`)](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [SLCTN-E01 — The map cannot be loaded for a selective run](layers/comando.md#slctn--runselection--a-run-takes-only-what-is-stale-and-below-the-minimum-unless-told-otherwise)

- [STEDS-B01 — The expired test evidence is listed before the stale edges, with a heading counting it and a closing note that expired evidence is not a test defect.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-B02 — Each expired evidence names its reason: the test file itself changed, or how many dependencies changed naming the first one, adding that the test itself changed too when both happened.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-B03 — Each stale edge is printed as its origin, type and destination with its reason, never validated when it has no stamp and advanced rev otherwise, followed by a summary counting each reason.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-B04 — When no edge is stale, it prints the clean message carrying the total number of edges.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-I01 — An edge stamped at the current revisions of both of its ends is never listed as stale.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-X01 — Reads the map and never writes it: no edge is stamped and no evidence is refreshed.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

- [STEDS-E01 — The map does not exist or cannot be read.](layers/comando.md#steds--staleedges--lists-the-confrontation-debt-expired-test-evidence-and-stale-edges)

### [CNSTC — StampCommand — writes the missing contract stamps on test doubles, and refreshes them after a change](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B01 — With no test named, every test of the map is considered, in sorted order; a test with nothing to stamp is not listed.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B02 — Writes the missing stamp above each double and lists, under the test, each stamp written and each double left unstamped with its reason, closing with the totals of stamps, files and doubles left unstamped.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B03 — The dry run says what it would write and leaves every file as it was.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B04 — The refresh lists each double stamped against the previous version of the file (test and line, member, old and new hash, and the block's lines that left and came since the last commit), updates their stamps and closes telling the user to adjust each double in the same commit.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B05 — The refresh of a file no double is stamped against says so and writes nothing.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B06 — When the stamped block has no version in the last commit, the refresh says there is nothing to compare instead of a diff.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B07 — The refresh in dry run lists the doubles and says nothing was written, leaving the stamps as they were.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B08 — The block diff lists the lines of the old block missing from the new one, marked as left, then the lines of the new block missing from the old one, marked as came, counting repeated lines.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-B09 — Handed a test file that holds stamps instead of a module, the refresh names the modules its stamps point at and the command to refresh them, and changes nothing.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-I01 — Stamping is idempotent: a second run over the same tests writes nothing.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-X01 — The plain form never rewrites an existing stamp, even one whose hash diverges from the module.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-E01 — The project has no configuration.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-E02 — The map does not exist or cannot be read.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-E03 — During a refresh, the member a stamp names no longer exists in the changed file.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [CNSTC-E04 — A test to stamp cannot be read.](layers/comando.md#cnstc--stampcommand--writes-the-missing-contract-stamps-on-test-doubles-and-refreshes-them-after-a-change)

- [PRSTP-B04 — A project with PROJECT.md and no configuration is sent to init, with the discovery shown as done.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B05 — A configured project with no map is sent to the map build.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B06 — The configuration is shown with its numbers of layers and gates and the map with its numbers of nodes and edges; informative gates clean everywhere are named as candidates for blocking.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B07 — The local queue shows the pending tasks and the issues in todo and doing, and names one next step in this order: finish the work in doing, pick from todo, take the next task, or nothing pending.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B08 — An assembled local project with no work is sent to the first plan.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B09 — The github queue names the repository and label and, when workflow pipelines are missing, stops at the doctor fix.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B10 — With the pipelines in place, the github queue states that work enters by pull request to the integration branch, and lists the protected branches when there is more than one.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B11 — The agent's own open cards, those whose last owner comment names this agent, are listed with number, title and state, and the agent is told to finish them instead of claiming new work.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B12 — Without an agent identity no card is attributed and the next step is to claim work.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-B13 — A github project whose map holds only guides is sent to the first plan before any card.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-I01 — Status never names a step beyond the first one missing.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-X01 — Status leaves the project as it found it: no file is created, changed or removed.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [PRSTP-E01 — The configuration file exists and does not load.](layers/comando.md#prstp--projectstatus--where-the-project-stands-in-the-cycle-and-the-one-next-step)

- [STPRS-B07 — The test command receives the code and test files of the impact path; the mutation command receives only the code files.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-B08 — A command declaring a target placeholder gets the given target in its place; a command without the placeholder is left as declared.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-B09 — After every suite passed, a chain naming coverage runs the coverage answer; an empty chain does nothing.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-B10 — An impact path with no code file runs nothing.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-B11 — After every suite passed, a chain naming check runs the check over the run's own scope: the changed files of an incremental run, the full sweep otherwise.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-B13 — A report whose modification time is up to two seconds before the run's start is this run's: a file system's clock is coarser than the process's (Linux stamps from a tick behind `now`, FAT to two seconds), and a report written in the run's first milliseconds must not read as older.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-E04 — Declared filters that match no suite together are refused.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-E05 — The command declares a target placeholder and no target was given.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

- [STPRS-E06 — Changed files were given and the suite declares no incremental command.](layers/comando.md#stprs--suiteproxy--runs-the-test-and-mutation-suites-the-project-declared-and-binds-their-reports-to-the-map)

### [HDTHD — HeaderDateTouch — bumps the header date of the files that changed, and only of those](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B01 — Only a date inside the header at the top of the file is bumped: a comment block containing the header marker within the first ten lines, in any comment dialect, or an HTML comment block that closes; header-like text elsewhere is not a header.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B06 — A staged file with changes outside the index is skipped, and its worktree change does not reach the index.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B07 — In a partial commit the real index is dated too.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B08 — The exclude globs of the flag and of the configuration add up.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B09 — The dry run says what it would bump and writes nothing.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

- [HDTHD-B10 — Each bump is listed with its old and new date and each skip with its reason, then the total.](layers/comando.md#hdthd--headerdatetouch--bumps-the-header-date-of-the-files-that-changed-and-only-of-those)

### [VPFVR — VerifyPhaseFacade — one invocation per phase, delegated to the check pipeline](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B01 — The staged scope is the files the index added, copied, modified or renamed; deletions and untracked files are not in it.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B02 — When nothing is staged, it says there is nothing to verify and succeeds.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B03 — Verify hands the files to the check command in a child process, one changed-file argument per file (or the full sweep).](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B04 — An automatic phase asks the check for the computable gates only and for the findings only.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B05 — The manual phase, or no phase, asks the check for the full report, judgment gates included.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B06 — The pre-commit phase over the index dates the staged files first and says which files it dated.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B07 — A project that turned pre-commit dating off gets no dating: the staged files keep their dates.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B08 — A staged file that also has changes outside the index is named as not dated.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B09 — The phase, the commit message file, the category, the skip-slow and the no-record choices reach the check unchanged.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B10 — A project root below the repository's top hands the check only its own staged files, named from the project root.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-B11 — Over the index (`--staged`), the check is asked to read the files as the index has them (`--index`), so an unstaged edit — another session's — cannot bar the commit; over the tree it is not. (`subArgs`)](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-I01 — The check is never asked for both the full sweep and a list of files.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-X01 — Verify holds no verdict of its own: what passes is what the check says passes.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-E01 — The child check exits with the not-governed code.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-E02 — The child check fails with any other code.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-E03 — Neither the staged scope, nor a file, nor the full sweep is given.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

- [VPFVR-E04 — The staged scope is asked for outside a git repository.](layers/comando.md#vpfvr--verifyphasefacade--one-invocation-per-phase-delegated-to-the-check-pipeline)

### [CLRTC — CliRoot — every command passes through one root that speaks the project's language and honours the freeze](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B01 — In a frozen project, a command outside the allowance is refused with a message naming the command and the freeze reason.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B02 — While frozen, thaw, freeze, status, doctor, guide, help, completion, coverage and impact still run.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B03 — A subcommand of an allowed command runs while frozen, because every command up the parent chain is checked.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B04 — A missing configuration, or one that does not load, is not frozen: the command proceeds.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B05 — The project read for the freeze and the language is the one `--root` points at, when the command has that flag.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B06 — A top-level `lang:` of the project is applied before the command runs, even when the rest of the file does not parse; a nested or unsupported `lang:` is ignored.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B07 — The root prints neither the error nor the usage of a failing command.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-B08 — The project's `lang:` is read from a line ending in `\r\n` as from one ending in `\n`.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-I01 — Every `anchors <command>` that the work guide and the pipeline workflows teach is a registered command.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-I02 — Every command that takes several files — a usage that names files and repeats them, such as `<file>...` — reads them as every other does, through `TakesFiles`: separate arguments or a comma-separated list.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

- [CLRTC-X01 — The freeze refusal is written in the project's language, not in the default one.](layers/comando.md#clrtc--cliroot--every-command-passes-through-one-root-that-speaks-the-projects-language-and-honours-the-freeze)

### [CMMRC — CommentMarkers — which text opens a line comment in each kind of file](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B01 — A known extension answers with all of its line-comment prefixes, in declared order (PHP accepts both the double slash and the hash) (`MarkersFor`).](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B02 — An unknown extension answers with no prefix at all, so the reader has no anchor to claim.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B03 — The comment used to write into a path follows the path's last extension, ignoring case: a test file named after its subject is the language of its last extension (`LineCommentFor`).](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B04 — A markup file (Markdown, HTML, XML) gets the opening of a block comment; closing it is the caller's job.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B05 — A path with no extension, or with one the table does not know, gets the hash comment.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-B06 — An extension with several prefixes gets the first one declared.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-I01 — For every extension in the table, the comment the writer uses is the first prefix the reader lists: reading and writing never disagree about a language.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CMMRC-X01 — The reader looks the extension up exactly as given: it neither lowers its case nor extracts it from a path.](layers/config.md#cmmrc--commentmarkers--which-text-opens-a-line-comment-in-each-kind-of-file)

- [CNFGO-B17 — A gate the catalog does not know loads exactly as declared.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B18 — A gate whose severity nobody declared does not block (`IsBlocking`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B19 — The scope is one run per target unless `batch` or `project` is declared; in a full scan the gate uses `scope_full` only when it is `batch` or `project`, and its ordinary scope otherwise (`EffectiveScope`, `ScopeForScan`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B20 — A gate with no phases runs in every phase; a gate with phases runs only in those it lists (`RunsIn`); an unnamed phase admits every gate except one declared for `manual` alone (`OnlyManual`), which runs only when the manual phase is asked for.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B21 — A gate takes part in both perspectives (change and all) unless `skip_on` lists the perspective (`SkipsOn`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B22 — The mutation report format is read from the `mutation-score` gate only, trimmed and lower-cased, and is the Mutation Testing Elements format when none is declared (`MutationFormat`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B23 — A gate checks the language of section titles unless it declares that check off (`ChecksSectionLanguage`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B24 — The integration branch is `main` when undeclared; the protected branches are the declared list, else the integration branch and `main` (only `main` when they are the same) (`IntegrationBranchOrDefault`, `ProtectedBranchesOrDefault`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B25 — A pull request needs one approval when the number is undeclared; a declared number, zero included, is kept (`RequiredApprovalsOrDefault`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B26 — A stale pipeline and an ingest run outside the test command only warn, unless the project declares that they block (`PipelineVelhoBarra`, `IngestManualBarra`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B27 — Only an explicit `enabled: false` freezes the project; an absent value, `true`, or a configuration that did not load does not (`Frozen`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B28 — The freeze reason is shown trimmed; a missing or blank reason is replaced by a message that asks for `freeze_reason` (`FreezeReasonText`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B29 — A section title comes from the layer's rename, then the project's, then the framework's default; a blank rename does not count (`SectionTitle`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B30 — The placeholder words are the declared ones, trimmed and without blanks, or the templates' single default marker word when none remain (`Placeholders`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B31 — The rule letters are the declared rule types' letters, upper-cased, one character each, without repeats, in declaration order; with none valid they are the canonical `SRVAXBNMDEIQWGP` (`RuleLetters`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B32 — A scenario tag maps to every letter whose rule type declares it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; a tag no rule type declares is reported as unknown (`TagLetters`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B33 — The code length pattern, placed after one character class, matches exactly the declared lengths: the one length, the contiguous range, or each of lengths that are not contiguous and nothing between them (`CodeLengthPattern`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B41 — A rule type catalogues a section when the section's title is one it declares as requiring a code, ignoring case and surrounding spaces (`RequiresCodeIn`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B34 — With no filter, every declared suite is selected; a suite with no workspace or no scope is not excluded by an axis nobody filtered (`SelecionaSuites`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B35 — The layer, workspace and scope filters each keep the suites that match one of their names, and the axes combine as an intersection.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B36 — The selected suites keep the order of the file, not the order of the request.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B37 — Names match ignoring case and surrounding spaces.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B38 — A requested name that no suite declares comes back labelled with its axis, all of them together; names that exist but never together are an empty selection, not a missing name.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B39 — The declared layers, workspaces and scopes are listed once each, in file order, leaving out the empty ones (`DeclaredLayers`, `DeclaredWorkspaces`, `DeclaredScopes`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-B40 — When the derived files declare `patterns`, those patterns become the code patterns, the other derived files are kept, and `patterns` never becomes a derived file of its own; without it the declared files are used as they are (`PadroesDe`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-I01 — What the configuration writer saves, the loader reads back with the same layers and gates (`Save`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-I02 — Refusing unknown keys never refuses a known one: a file that uses only declared keys loads complete.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-I03 — Every reader of the configuration answers its default on a configuration or workflow that is absent, never a failure (`GitHubMode`, `ManualMode`, `RouteRegistry`).](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-X01 — Does not infer the GitHub repository from the git remote.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-X02 — Does not validate suite layer, workspace or scope names against a fixed list.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E01 — The configuration file cannot be read.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E02 — The path the configuration is saved to cannot be written.](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E03 — REF[CNFGO-B01]: an unknown key is the refusal B01 states: the load fails naming the key](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E04 — REF[CNFGO-B06]: a repeated gate ID is the refusal B06 states: the load fails naming both gates](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E05 — REF[CNFGO-B07]: a gate enum outside its list is the refusal B07 states](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E06 — REF[CNFGO-B09]: an incomplete GitHub workflow is the refusal B09 states](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E07 — REF[CNFGO-B10]: an unknown workflow mode is the refusal B10 states](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

- [CNFGO-E09 — REF[CNFGO-B12]: an unsupported language is the refusal B12 states](layers/config.md#cnfgo--config--loads-the-projects-anchorsyaml-refuses-what-it-cannot-honour-and-answers-every-setting-with-its-default)

### [CNTNR — Containers — what runs separately, and which layers run inside each](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B01 — The declared containers come back as written, with their talks; a missing configuration has none.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B02 — The internal containers are the declared ones without the external ones, in declared order (`InternalContainers`).](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B03 — A layer is found in the container that declares it, ignoring case and the spaces around the declared name (`ContainerOfLayer`).](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B04 — A layer no container claims has no container, and that is an answer, not an error.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B05 — The layers of an external container are still claimed by it.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B06 — The orphan layers are the given ones that no container claims, in the order they were given (`OrphanLayers`).](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-B07 — A layer the Estrutura declares with a kind other than `code` — spec, feature, test, doc, guide, plan — runs nowhere by nature and is never an orphan; a layer the Estrutura does not declare, or declares with no kind, stays in. The name is matched ignoring case.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-I01 — A layer that runs code is an orphan exactly when it has no container: the two answers never disagree about the same layer.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

- [CNTNR-X01 — With no container declared, no layer is placed by guessing: every layer is an orphan.](layers/config.md#cntnr--containers--what-runs-separately-and-which-layers-run-inside-each)

### [DLCTI — Dialect — the lexicon of the project's language, between an agnostic gate and concrete code](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B01 — A project that declares no dialect gets only the naming defaults: no language lexicon at all.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B02 — The family fills every lexicon field the project left empty, and a field the project declared wins over the family (`DialectFor`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B03 — The family name is matched ignoring case.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B04 — An unknown family contributes nothing; the known families are listed in alphabetical order for the messages that name them (`KnownDialectFamilies`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B05 — The two naming conventions (the set-promise and the set-slice verbs) apply whatever the family, and a declared one replaces its default.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B06 — The Gherkin language defaults to English and is looked up ignoring case, answering the table's own spelling of the code, so `PT` is `pt` and `zh-cn` is `zh-CN`; a language outside the table keeps its code as declared and gets the English keywords (`GherkinFor`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B07 — The recognised ways to open a scenario are those of every language in the table — scenario, outline and synonyms — each once, longest first, so an outline that contains the word for scenario is tried before it (`GherkinScenarioAlternatives`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B08 — The recognised result keywords are those of every language in the table, in alphabetical order (`GherkinThenAlternatives`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B09 — An empty or invalid pattern compiles to nothing, which the gates read as "not declared" (`Compile`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B10 — A lexicon field is waived only when the opt-out list names it by its configuration name, ignoring case and spaces; its name in the code does not waive it (`WaivedField`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B11 — The default set-promise convention recognises the verb after a provider prefix (a cloud-provider list call) and never inside another word (allocate, callback, enlistment).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B12 — The default set-slice convention is a query verb opening the name, followed by a slice word (first, recent, top, page…).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B13 — The Go family recognises both shapes of error handling: `if err != nil` and `if err := f(); err != nil`. The second is the commoner, and matching only the first left the handling of most Go code invisible to the failure gates.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B20 — Each language family declares how its code reads an environment variable (`env_read`), capturing the name; the project's own pattern wins, and with no family declared `EnvReadPattern` is every family's together.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B19 — The Go family also sees an error held in a field and a sentinel error: `if result.Error != nil` and `return ErrNotFound` handle a failure, and `return nil, result.Error` and `return ErrNotFound` propagate it, which records it as `fmt.Errorf` does; `return e.Error()`, which turns the error into text, propagates nothing.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B14 — The Go and TS families say how a test is written — Go by `t.Run(`, TS by `it`/`test`/`describe`, also as `.only`, `.skip` or `.each(table)` — and a project that declares its own `tests` keeps it over the family's.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B15 — The TS family recognises a `catch` as handling a failure with or without its binding: `catch (e) {` and `catch {`.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B16 — The Go and TS families say what an assertion is (`tests.assertion`). A project that declares only its assertion keeps the family's way to open a test; one that declares its own pattern or script reads its tests another way and does not take the family's assertion.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B17 — The Go, TS and Python families say how code defines a name (`definition`) — Go's functions, methods and types, TS's functions, classes and constants bound to an arrow function, Python's `def` and `class` — and a declared one wins over the family's. A capture group named `owner` is the type a member belongs to, not the name: Go's captures a method's receiver type.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-B18 — The recognised keywords that open an outline's examples are those of every language in the table, each once, in alphabetical order (`GherkinExamplesAlternatives`).](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-I01 — Every pattern a built-in family or a naming default brings compiles. A built-in pattern that did not compile would be read as undeclared, and the gate would approve in silence.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-I02 — The keywords written for any language of the table are among those every reader recognises.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-X01 — No family brings a collection query: that pattern is always the project's to declare.](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

- [DLCTI-E01 — REF[DLCTI-B09]: a pattern that does not compile is the failure B09 absorbs: it compiles to nothing, and the gate answers as for an undeclared pattern](layers/config.md#dlcti--dialect--the-lexicon-of-the-projects-language-between-an-agnostic-gate-and-concrete-code)

### [DCRQA — DocsRequired — which aggregate documentation a change of a unit obliges to touch](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B01 — A trigger naming a layer charges every change in that layer, whatever the unit (`TriggeredBy`).](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B02 — A trigger naming a unit code charges that unit, and not its neighbours in the same layer.](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B03 — Asked without a unit code, the answer is the layer's alone: no code trigger, not even a blank one, can match an absent code (`RequiredFor`).](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B04 — A documentation with no trigger is never owed by a unit change.](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B05 — A trigger matches ignoring case and the spaces around it.](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-B06 — Every declared documentation can be listed; a project with no docs block, or no configuration, owes none and lists none (`AllRequiredDocs`).](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-I01 — Naming the unit never removes a documentation the layer alone owes: the answer with a code contains the answer without one.](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

- [DCRQA-X01 — A trigger is matched whole, never as part of a longer or shorter name.](layers/config.md#dcrqa--docsrequired--which-aggregate-documentation-a-change-of-a-unit-obliges-to-touch)

### [MNVRM — MinVersion — whether the running binary meets the minimum version the project declares](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B01 — Versions are ordered part by part as numbers: major over minor over patch, and 9 is smaller than 84 (`VersionOrder`).](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B02 — The tag prefix v is accepted on either side.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B03 — With no minimum declared, any running binary meets it, whatever it reports (`AtendeMinVersion`).](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B04 — A running version that cannot be ordered (`dev`, empty, not three numeric parts) does not meet a declared minimum, and the reason is returned.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B05 — A declared minimum that is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH is refused when the configuration loads, `dev` and pre-releases included.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B06 — An absent minimum, or a well-formed one with or without the tag prefix, is accepted.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-B07 — The refusal names the expected format, gives an example, quotes the value, and says a value that cannot be compared silences the warning the field exists to give.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-I01 — The order is antisymmetric: swapping the two versions always flips the answer, and only equal versions compare as equal.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-X01 — A pre-release is never compared as if it were its final release.](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-E01 — REF[MNVRM-B05]: a malformed declared minimum is the load failure B05 answers: the configuration does not load](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

- [MNVRM-E02 — REF[MNVRM-B04]: a running version that cannot be ordered is the comparison failure B04 answers: it does not meet the minimum, with the reason](layers/config.md#mnvrm--minversion--whether-the-running-binary-meets-the-minimum-version-the-project-declares)

### [DRPTD — DerivedPatterns — a derived file declared as one pattern or as a list of them](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-B01 — A single pattern written as text becomes a list of one (`UnmarshalYAML`).](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-B02 — A list of patterns is kept whole and in order.](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-B03 — An empty list is refused, and the refusal names the cause and the two ways out: declare one, or remove the layer.](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-B04 — Any shape other than text or a list of texts is refused.](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-B05 — Written back, one pattern is text and several are a list (`MarshalYAML`).](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-I01 — What is written back reads back as the same patterns, in the same order.](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-X01 — The patterns are kept exactly as written: this unit neither expands them, trims them, nor checks them as patterns.](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-E01 — REF[DRPTD-B03]: an empty list is the shape failure B03 refuses, naming the cause](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

- [DRPTD-E02 — REF[DRPTD-B04]: a mapping or a list of mappings is the shape failure B04 refuses](layers/config.md#drptd--derivedpatterns--a-derived-file-declared-as-one-pattern-or-as-a-list-of-them)

### [PRRPR — ProjectRootResolution — the project root a command works on](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

- [PRRPR-B01 — The project root is the nearest directory, from the start upwards, that holds the configuration file; a project nested in another is its own.](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

- [PRRPR-B02 — With no project above the start, the start comes back unchanged, relative if it was relative.](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

- [PRRPR-B03 — With no root given (empty or `.`), the root is found by walking up from the working directory (`AbsRoot`).](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

- [PRRPR-I01 — The resolved root is always absolute, even outside any project.](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

- [PRRPR-X01 — An explicit root is made absolute and never walked above, even when a directory above it holds a project.](layers/config.md#prrpr--projectrootresolution--the-project-root-a-command-works-on)

### [GTVCG — GateVocabulary — the list of default gate names, injected into the configuration layer](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

- [GTVCG-B01 — With no source registered, the default gate names are absent, and asking is not a failure (`DefaultGateNamesForTest`).](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

- [GTVCG-B02 — With a source registered, the default gate names are the ones it gives.](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

- [GTVCG-B03 — The letters of the artifacts that are not specs are fixed and English: a plan's phase is `W`, a flow's step `T`, an action's result `O`, and none is a canonical spec letter with another meaning; the phase letter is among the canonical rule letters, since specs cite phases in `needs:` (`PhaseLetter`, `StepLetter`, `OutcomeLetter`).](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

- [GTVCG-I01 — The answer always comes from the source registered last: registering again replaces the previous source.](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

- [GTVCG-X01 — The names are not cached: each question asks the registered source again.](layers/config.md#gtvcg--gatevocabulary--the-list-of-default-gate-names-injected-into-the-configuration-layer)

## doct

### [DCENV — Environment — the project's environment variables page, compiled from its specs](layers/doct.md#dcenv--environment--the-projects-environment-variables-page-compiled-from-its-specs)

- [DCENV-B01 — `envVars` lists every variable the specs declare, read under the section's title and columns in any language of the catalog, ordered by name; a `TODO` placeholder is no variable.](layers/doct.md#dcenv--environment--the-projects-environment-variables-page-compiled-from-its-specs)

- [DCENV-B02 — A variable declared by several specs is listed once, with every unit that declares it, and the first description given.](layers/doct.md#dcenv--environment--the-projects-environment-variables-page-compiled-from-its-specs)

- [DCENV-B03 — `ScaffoldEnvironment`: The environment page template, in the project's language, renders one table row per variable with the units that read it; init writes it when a spec declares a variable.](layers/doct.md#dcenv--environment--the-projects-environment-variables-page-compiled-from-its-specs)

- [DCENV-E01 — A row has no variable name, or carries the template's `TODO` placeholder.](layers/doct.md#dcenv--environment--the-projects-environment-variables-page-compiled-from-its-specs)

### [OPNAP — OpenAPI — the project's API document, compiled from the specs of its API units](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-B01 — Each Endpoint row of a spec is an operation under its path and method, with the operation name, the spec's title as summary and its overview as description, `deprecated` when the row says so, and the spec's parameters, body, responses (a range `4xx` as `4XX`), the error codes and messages of `Error Responses` under each one's status, its security schemes and its limits.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-B02 — A contract cited by the body or a response is a shared schema named after the contract's spec file, built from its Domain — one property per input, the type from `Type`, the required ones from `Required`, what it accepts as the description —, whatever language the section and its columns are written in.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-B03 — The document's keys come in OpenAPI's order and are indented by two spaces; a response with no contract has no content.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-B04 — The compiled YAML opens with the generated marker as a `#` comment, and is valid YAML.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-B05 — A compiled YAML is recognised as generated — overwritten, never skipped — and goes stale when a spec it reads changes.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-E01 — A Contract cell cites no spec's code, or a code no spec of the project has.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

- [OPNAP-E02 — An Endpoint row has no method or no path.](layers/doct.md#opnap--openapi--the-projects-api-document-compiled-from-the-specs-of-its-api-units)

## gate

### [APISP — APISpec — the coherence of an API spec, and its error codes in the code](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B01 — A node that is not code and a code file whose spec is missing or has no `Endpoint` leave every gate without a verdict.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B02 — `api-contracts-resolve` fails naming each body or response (by status) whose contract is empty or `TODO`, each cited code no spec of the map carries, and each contract whose spec has no Domain table; `—` is a response with no body.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B03 — `api-errors-declared` fails naming each error response whose status the Responses do not declare — exactly, or by its range (`4xx`) —, and each one without an error code or a message; a spec with no error response leaves without a verdict.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B04 — `error-codes-honored` fails naming each declared error code that appears in none of the unit's code — the main file and the files its spec specifies, comments removed —, and the files it read.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B06 — `SetProjectSectionTitles`: The titles the project's `section_titles` give a catalog section — its own and each layer's — are found as that section too, besides the catalog's translations.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-B05 — Sections are found under their title in any language of the catalog, and their columns by their header in those languages.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-E01 — The spec beside the code file cannot be read, or there is none.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

- [APISP-E02 — A contract's spec or one of the unit's code files cannot be read.](camadas/gate.md#apisp--apispec--the-coherence-of-an-api-spec-and-its-error-codes-in-the-code)

### [BRCOV — BranchCoverage — the tests take the branches the code has](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

- [BRCOV-B01 — A file whose share of branches taken is below the floor fails, naming the share, the floor, the branches missed out of the total and their lines in order; at or above the floor it passes. With no `min_percent` the floor is 100: every branch.](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

- [BRCOV-B02 — A branch on a line carrying `@no-branch: <why>`, or on the line after it, is left out of the missed; a waiver with no reason waives nothing.](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

- [BRCOV-B03 — A missed branch on a line where the mutation, measured at the node's revision, found a mutant no test ran fails as likely dead, naming the lines — whatever the floor. A mutation measured at another revision says nothing about these lines.](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

- [BRCOV-B04 — A node that is not code is skipped; a node with no coverage, or coverage of another revision, is pending; a coverage with no branch is skipped.](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

- [BRCOV-B05 — A file a coverage report listed with no instrumentable line is skipped, and one a whole run of its suite left out of the report is a divergence, as `line-coverage` reads them. (`coverageAbsence`)](camadas/gate.md#brcov--branchcoverage--the-tests-take-the-branches-the-code-has)

### [CDCTC — CodeCataloged — what the code EXPORTS must be in the spec, or waived in the code](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B01 — An artifact that is not a spec leaves without a verdict: the ruler starts from the spec that governs the code.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B02 — An exported symbol the spec never names FAILS, and the verdict names the orphan and its LINE — the name alone would make the reader hunt for the symbol.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B03 — What the spec already catalogues is never accused.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B04 — `@no-rule: <reason>` on the symbol waives it: not every export deserves a rule, and the waiver is what makes the noise manageable without lying.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B05 — A BARE marker, with no written reason, does not waive — it would be a silent way to quiet the gate, and the trace that a decision was taken would vanish.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B06 — A spec cataloguing every exported symbol passes.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B07 — With no code linked the gate leaves without a verdict: the absence belongs to `unit-complete`, and accusing it in both places would duplicate the debt.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B08 — Without a declared export pattern the gate SKIPS and says it skipped, naming how to enable it. It never approves what it cannot read.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B09 — With the pattern declared the gate confronts for real, in any language — the project's own `export_detect` is the ruler.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B10 — The declared dialect family also supplies the pattern: a Go project needs only name its family.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-B11 — Every file the spec governs (`specifies`) is confronted, not only the first; the verdict names the files that hold orphans, and when more than one does, each orphan carries its file beside its line.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-I01 — The waiver holds in the COMMENT BLOCK above the symbol, not only on its own line. The declaration is documentation: whoever writes it puts the explanation alongside, and the explanation rarely fits on one line. Looking only at `i-1` made the gate ignore the declaration and keep accusing — measured in a file where it sat on the second line of a two-line comment.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-I02 — The waiver does NOT leak between symbols. A symbol with no comment above it does not inherit another symbol's declaration — inheriting would let one marker exempt the whole file, which is the opposite of what it is.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-I03 — Green over what was never read is the worst possible failure in a measuring instrument. Not knowing how to read is a reason to go quiet and SAY SO, never to approve — and never silently, because the bias of the built-in ecosystem would hide inside that silence.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-X01 — Does not judge whether the catalogued rule DESCRIBES the symbol well.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-X02 — Does not decide which symbols deserve a rule.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-X03 — Does not know any language: whoever declares what is public is the project.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-X04 — Does not charge the absence of code — that belongs to `unit-complete`.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-E01 — No map has been built when the gate confronts a spec.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-E02 — A code file the spec `specifies` is no longer on disk.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

- [CDCTC-E03 — `derived.export_detect` is declared but has no capture group.](camadas/gate.md#cdctc--codecataloged--what-the-code-exports-must-be-in-the-spec-or-waived-in-the-code)

### [CDLNG — CodeLanguage — the code does not go back to mixing languages](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B01 — An identifier in Portuguese is ACCUSED; an identifier in English passes without noise.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B02 — The verdict RETURNS the word that accused — without it, whoever reads looks for the needle in the whole file.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B03 — Only a DECLARATION is the subject: what does not declare an identifier is not read.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B04 — The declarations are truly found, in every form the language offers — not only in the most common one. `PortugueseIdentifiers` sweeps the content and returns what accused.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B05 — `WordIsPortuguese` decides ONE word, and `IdentifierIsPortuguese` decides a whole identifier by breaking it into the words that compose it — it is the separation that lets the length floor hold per word, and not for the whole identifier.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B06 — The project's own production code declares no identifier this ruler accuses: every Go file outside tests, vendored code and test data is swept, and each accusation names the identifier, the word that caused it and the file.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-B07 — No gate of this package decides by confronting prose in the team's language: the text a gate matches is stable vocabulary — a marker, a code or the document's structure — so translating the project never silences a gate.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-I01 — A short word does not count. Below the length floor there is no language to infer, and accusing there would be noise — which is how a gate loses the trust of whoever reads it.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-X01 — Does not read a COMMENT.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-X02 — Does not read USER-FACING TEXT.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

- [CDLNG-X03 — Does not use a dictionary to decide the language.](camadas/gate.md#cdlng--codelanguage--the-code-does-not-go-back-to-mixing-languages)

### [CRVCD — CodeReferenceValid — cross-referenced requirement codes must resolve to existing units](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B01 — When the confronted node kind is not a specification, the gate skips confrontation.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B02 — When the map graph is nil, confrontation returns a pending verdict because external identities cannot be resolved.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B03 — When the map graph contains no declared identity codes, confrontation returns pending rather than approving blindly.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B04 — When all cited external requirement codes resolve to known units in the map graph, the gate passes.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B05 — When a specification cites an external requirement code whose unit is not in the map graph, the gate fails.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B06 — Citations matching the specification's own identity code are recognized as self-references and are not charged as orphans.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B07 — Multiple orphaned requirement codes are reported in alphabetical order formatted as identifiers.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B08 — Identity ownership is determined from graph node metadata and specification header comments on disk.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-B09 — Text tokens that do not match requirement code structure are ignored and never charged as external references.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-I01 — A specification is sovereign over its own identity code, so internal cross-references to its own requirements never fail.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-I02 — An absent map graph or an empty identity universe always yields Pending, never Pass, refusing to approve what cannot be measured.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-I03 — Any unresolvable external requirement citation produces a blocking Fail verdict.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-X01 — Does not evaluate whether the referenced requirement behavior is implemented correctly.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-X02 — Does not inspect non-specification artifacts like code or tests for dangling requirement citations.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-X03 — Does not mandate that a specification must cite external requirements.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

- [CRVCD-E01 — A spec the map carries without its code is no longer on disk, so its header cannot be read when the declared codes are collected.](camadas/gate.md#crvcd--codereferencevalid--cross-referenced-requirement-codes-must-resolve-to-existing-units)

### [CTRIM — ContractImpact — a changed field names the rules that use it, and their tests](camadas/gate.md#ctrim--contractimpact--a-changed-field-names-the-rules-that-use-it-and-their-tests)

- [CTRIM-B01 — A field whose row differs from the spec at HEAD, or that HEAD had and the spec no longer has, is changed; a field only the new version has is not. (`ContractImpacts`, `Impact`)](camadas/gate.md#ctrim--contractimpact--a-changed-field-names-the-rules-that-use-it-and-their-tests)

- [CTRIM-B02 — A changed field names the rules that use it — by name or first segment — in this spec and in the specs that depend on the code it governs, and the test files whose titles cite those rules; a changed field no rule uses names nothing.](camadas/gate.md#ctrim--contractimpact--a-changed-field-names-the-rules-that-use-it-and-their-tests)
