- [VLANV-X02 — A literal nobody declared is not charged.](camadas/gate.md#vlanv--valueanchored--a-replicated-key-is-declared-where-it-is-used-and-every-copy-carries-the-same-value)

- [VLANV-X03 — Does not decide the anchor's syntax.](camadas/gate.md#vlanv--valueanchored--a-replicated-key-is-declared-where-it-is-used-and-every-copy-carries-the-same-value)

- [VLANV-E01 — A spec the map lists is no longer on disk when the project index is built.](camadas/gate.md#vlanv--valueanchored--a-replicated-key-is-declared-where-it-is-used-and-every-copy-carries-the-same-value)

- [VLANV-E02 — A code file the map lists is no longer on disk when the project index is built.](camadas/gate.md#vlanv--valueanchored--a-replicated-key-is-declared-where-it-is-used-and-every-copy-carries-the-same-value)

- [VLANV-E03 — `derived.value_anchor` is declared with fewer than two capture groups.](camadas/gate.md#vlanv--valueanchored--a-replicated-key-is-declared-where-it-is-used-and-every-copy-carries-the-same-value)

## infra

### [CHRCC — ChangeRecord — the delivery record an agent leaves when it finishes a stage](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B01 — The key of a record is its stage, two hyphens, its unit with the extension dropped and every `/`, `\`, space and `.` turned into a hyphen (leading and trailing hyphens trimmed), a hyphen, and the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the unit with `\` written as `/`.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B02 — A record waiting for review lives at `changes/<key>.md` under the project root.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B03 — The rendered record opens with an @anchors header of layer `change` carrying the stage, the unit and the date; the agent line is written only when an agent is named.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B04 — The rendered record states the delivery title, the intent (trimmed) under "What was done", and one line per touched file under "Files".](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B05 — The "Decisions the ruler did not decide" and "What is NOT proven" sections are always written: an empty one carries the sentence that says so ("none — …", "nothing — …") instead of being omitted.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B06 — Saving writes the rendered record at its path, creating `changes/` when missing; saving a second delivery with the same stage and unit replaces the first. (`Save`)](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B07 — The pending list holds only the `.md` files directly inside `changes/`, sorted, and is empty (without error) when the folder does not exist.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B08 — Marking a record reviewed moves it, under the same file name, to `changes/reviewed/`, creating that folder when missing. (`MarkReviewed`)](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B09 — When the history already holds a record of that file name, the reviewed record takes the first free name `<key>.<n>.md` (n from 2), so every earlier review stays.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-B10 — In the header and the title, a line break in the stage, unit, date or agent is written escaped (`\n`, `\r`) and `-->` is written `-- >`, so no field can add a header line or close the header.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-I01 — A reviewed record is never lost: after the move it is no longer pending and it exists in the history.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-I02 — Two different units never share a key; the two separator spellings of one unit do.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-X01 — The pending list does not descend into subfolders, so the reviewed history (or any folder named like a record) is never listed as pending.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-E01 — `changes/` exists but cannot be read as a folder (for example, it is a file).](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-E02 — `changes/` cannot be created when a record is saved.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

- [CHRCC-E03 — The record to mark reviewed no longer exists.](layers/infra.md#chrcc--changerecord--the-delivery-record-an-agent-leaves-when-it-finishes-a-stage)

### [CHNGL — Changelog — the releases of a project, read from its commits](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B01 — A commit that declares a breaking change — a `!` after the type, or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer — goes to the breaking changes whatever its type, and the footer's text is added to its subject (`Classify`).](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B02 — A `feat` goes to the features, with its scope and short hash.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B03 — A `fix` with a `Bug:` footer goes to the bugs fixed, carrying where the bug was seen; a `fix` without it goes to the fixes.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B04 — A commit of another type, or outside Conventional Commits, is left out; a release with nothing listed is empty.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B05 — Footers are the paragraphs at the end of the body made only of `Key: value` lines, read from the last one back — a `Bug:` block followed by a `Co-Authored-By:` block is still the footer —; a `Bug:` line in a paragraph of prose, or before one, is not a footer (`FooterLines`).](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B06 — The tags reachable from a ref are listed in version order, and each release holds the commits after the previous tag of that whole list, oldest first; the releases come back newest first.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B07 — With `unreleased`, what came after the last tag becomes a release with no version, on top.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B08 — The built-in template writes the version and date, or the translated "unreleased" heading, and one translated section per non-empty group; a bug entry ends with where it was seen.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B09 — A release written into an incremental file starts with a marker naming its version (`Marker`), and `Written` lists the versions a file holds by those markers.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B10 — Writing puts the releases the file does not hold on its top, below a leading `# ` title, and keeps everything else as it was, hand edits included; a release the file holds is not written again (`Prepend`).](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B11 — The unreleased block a previous write left is replaced by the new one, up to the next marker.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B12 — An empty file gets the given title before the releases.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-B13 — The markers of a changelog with CRLF line endings are found as in one with LF.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-E01 — The template does not parse, or fails while rendering.](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

- [CHNGL-E02 — A git command fails (not a repository, an unknown ref).](layers/infra.md#chngl--changelog--the-releases-of-a-project-read-from-its-commits)

### [CHLGC — CheckLog — the check's output mirrored to a file, so it can be reread without re-running](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B01 — The full check is mirrored to `.anchors/check-all.txt` and the changed-files check to `.anchors/check-changed.txt`. (`ScopeName`)](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B02 — The header is written first, then everything the command writes to standard output is copied to the file.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B03 — An output longer than the pipe's buffer is copied whole, and closing the mirror does not hang.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B04 — When the mirror file cannot be opened, no mirror is returned, closing it and asking its path are safe (the path is empty), and standard output stays usable.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B05 — The header records the command, the moment it ran (date, time and offset) and, when a HEAD is known, the HEAD with its subject; with no HEAD, no HEAD line is written. (`Header`)](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-B06 — The tree line reads `clean` for zero modified files, `1 modified file` for one, and `N modified file(s)` for more.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-I01 — The two scopes never overwrite each other: a changed-files check leaves the full snapshot intact.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-X01 — The header never claims a clean tree it could not count: a negative count reads `unknown`.](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

- [CHLGC-E01 — REF[CHLGC-B04]: the state folder or the mirror file cannot be created, which B04 answers by running the check without a mirror](layers/infra.md#chlgc--checklog--the-checks-output-mirrored-to-a-file-so-it-can-be-reread-without-re-running)

### [CDGNC — CodeGenerator — the short, stable identity code suggested for a unit's name](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B01 — A generic suffix (Screen, Component, Modal, Sheet, Layout, Overlay, View, Page) is removed before compressing; a name that is only the suffix is kept whole. (`StripGeneric`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B02 — The name is split into words at `-`, `_` and spaces, where a lowercase letter or a digit meets an uppercase letter, and between an acronym and the capitalised word after it.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B03 — A name with at least as many words as the code length takes the initials of its first words. (`Generate`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B04 — A name of two words up to one fewer than the code length gives each word the same share of letters (its initial, then its consonants), and any slot left is filled from the joined words, consonants first.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B05 — A single word gives its consonants in order, then its vowels and digits, so a word that starts with a vowel does not start its code with it.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B06 — The code is upper case, padded with X up to the code length; padding an existing code applies the same rule and cuts it to the code length. (`Pad`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B07 — With a module prefix, the code starts with the prefix in upper case (cut to the code length) and the rest comes from the name's initial and consonants. (`GenerateWithPrefix`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B08 — A code not taken is returned as generated; a taken one is varied deterministically, trying every other letter in the last position, then in the one before, never changing the positions of the module prefix. (`GenerateUnique`, `GenerateUniqueWithPrefix`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B09 — The module prefix of a module name is its initial and its first consonant, padded with X to two characters. (`ModulePrefix`)](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-B10 — The generated length is the smallest declared code length of at least 2; loading the project's configuration applies it, and an empty list leaves the length unchanged.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-I01 — The same name and the same taken codes always give the same code, and a resolved collision is never a taken code.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

- [CDGNC-X01 — Does not guarantee a free code when every variation is taken: it then returns the generated code, taken as it is.](layers/infra.md#cdgnc--codegenerator--the-short-stable-identity-code-suggested-for-a-units-name)

### [CFPCD — CodeFromPath — the most meaningful unique code for a unit, given its file path](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

- [CFPCD-B01 — The generic file names are handler, index, resource, mod, main, types, route, routes, schema and config, recognised in any letter case. (`IsGenericBasename`)](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

- [CFPCD-B02 — A unit whose file name is generic takes its code from its parent folder's name; one with no parent folder keeps its own name. (`GenerateFromPath`)](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

- [CFPCD-B03 — The unit's base name drops `.spec.md`, `.feature`, or everything from `.test.` on, and otherwise the extension, so every artifact of a unit compresses the same name.](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

- [CFPCD-B04 — A file name that is not generic gives the generator's code for that name when it is free.](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

- [CFPCD-I01 — Two units with the same base name get different codes, and the same path with the same taken codes gets the same code.](layers/infra.md#cfpcd--codefrompath--the-most-meaningful-unique-code-for-a-unit-given-its-file-path)

### [DMSTD — DaemonState — the background watcher's state files: PID, pause flag, log and meta](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B01 — The state files are `.anchors/watch.pid`, `watch.log`, `watch.paused` and `watch.meta` under the project root. (`PathsFor`)](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B02 — "Running" answers the PID written in the PID file when that process is alive, and 0 when the file is missing, not a positive integer, or points at no live process. (`WritePID`)](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B03 — A PID file pointing at a process that has exited is removed when "running" is asked.](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B04 — Stopping when no watcher is running is refused with "watcher is not running".](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B05 — Stopping a running watcher terminates its process and removes the PID file.](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B06 — The watcher is paused exactly while the pause flag file exists: pausing creates it and resuming removes it. (`Pause`, `Resume`, `IsPaused`)](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B07 — Cleanup removes the PID file and the pause flag.](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-B08 — The meta file holds `started=` with the start moment in RFC 3339 and `root=` with the project root, one per line; reading a missing meta gives empty text. (`WriteMeta`, `ReadMeta`)](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-I01 — A PID file never outlives the answer "not running" for an exited process: after the check, the file is gone.](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-E01 — REF[DMSTD-B04]: stopping with no watcher is the failure B04 answers with "watcher is not running"](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

- [DMSTD-E02 — The state folder cannot be created when the PID is written.](layers/infra.md#dmstd--daemonstate--the-background-watchers-state-files-pid-pause-flag-log-and-meta)

### [DMRND — DaemonRuntime — how each platform probes and terminates the background watcher](layers/infra.md#dmrnd--daemonruntime--how-each-platform-probes-and-terminates-the-background-watcher)

- [DMRND-B01 — A process that exists is reported alive, and one that has exited is reported not alive.](layers/infra.md#dmrnd--daemonruntime--how-each-platform-probes-and-terminates-the-background-watcher)

- [DMRND-B02 — On Unix-like systems, terminating sends SIGTERM, a signal the watcher can catch to exit cleanly, not an uncatchable kill.](layers/infra.md#dmrnd--daemonruntime--how-each-platform-probes-and-terminates-the-background-watcher)

- [DMRND-B03 — On Unix-like systems, a process the probe may not signal (the probe answers "operation not permitted", EPERM) exists, so it is reported alive: a live watcher of another user is never taken for a stale one.](layers/infra.md#dmrnd--daemonruntime--how-each-platform-probes-and-terminates-the-background-watcher)

- [DMRND-I01 — Whatever the platform's termination does, stopping the watcher leaves no PID file behind: the removal does not depend on the watcher's loop running its cleanup.](layers/infra.md#dmrnd--daemonruntime--how-each-platform-probes-and-terminates-the-background-watcher)

### [GTAVG — GitAvailability — why a git operation cannot happen, named with its fix](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B01 — When `git` is not on the PATH, the answer is "no git binary", whatever the folder holds. (`Check`)](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B02 — With git on the PATH, a `.git` entry in the root or in any ancestor folder makes the answer "available".](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B03 — With git on the PATH and no `.git` entry up to the filesystem root, the answer is "no repository".](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B04 — The explanation for "no git binary" names the action and says git is not installed (or not on the PATH), and never sends the user to `git init`. (`Explain`)](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B05 — The explanation for "no repository" names the action and sends the user to `git init`, and never says git is missing.](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-B06 — When git is available the explanation is empty, so no git cause is invented for a failure of another kind.](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-E01 — REF[GTAVG-B01]: git missing from the PATH is the failure B01 classifies, with its fix in B04](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

- [GTAVG-E02 — REF[GTAVG-B03]: a root outside any repository is the failure B03 classifies, with its fix in B05](layers/infra.md#gtavg--gitavailability--why-a-git-operation-cannot-happen-named-with-its-fix)

### [GTMTG — GitMeta — what git knows about the files: last commit dates, pending changes, HEAD, dirty count](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B01 — Today is the system date as year-month-day.](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B02 — The last commit date of a file is the day (year-month-day) of the most recent commit that touched it; a file never committed, or a root outside a repository, gives no date. (`LastCommitDate`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B03 — The bulk date reader gives, for every file of the repository, the day of the most recent commit that touched it, and an empty map outside a repository. (`AllCommitDates`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B04 — The pending-change question answers whether the file has uncommitted edits (a new or edited file has them, a just-committed file does not), together with whether the question could be asked at all. (`UncommittedChanges`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B05 — The yes/no pending-change shortcut answers yes for a new or edited file in a repository and no for a just-committed one. (`HasUncommittedChanges`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B06 — HEAD is the short hash and the subject of the last commit; it is not known outside a repository or in a repository with no commit. (`Head`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B07 — The dirty count is the number of files with uncommitted changes in the whole tree: 0 in a clean repository, 1 after one new file. (`DirtyCount`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B08 — A file's content at the last commit is returned as HEAD has it; a file HEAD does not have, or a directory that is not a repository, has none. (`AtHead`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-B09 — Whether the commit being made changes a file is read from the index: a staged edit or an added file does, an unstaged edit does not; outside a repository it cannot be told. (`StagedChanges`)](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-X01 — The dirty count never answers 0 when it could not count: outside a repository or without git it answers a negative number.](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-X02 — The pending-change question never answers "known" when it could not ask: outside a repository it answers not known and no change.](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-E01 — REF[GTMTG-X01]: git failing to list the tree's status is the failure X01 answers with a negative count](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

- [GTMTG-E02 — REF[GTMTG-X02]: git failing to report a file's status is the failure X02 answers with "not known"](layers/infra.md#gtmtg--gitmeta--what-git-knows-about-the-files-last-commit-dates-pending-changes-head-dirty-count)

### [APRCP — ApprovalReachable — the doctor says when the required approval can never be given, and how to get out](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B01 — `CanBypassProtection`: The current account can bypass the protection only when it is an administrator of the repository AND the protection does not enforce its rules on administrators.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B02 — Each refusal of the bypass names its reason: the platform CLI is missing, the current user cannot be read, the account is not an administrator (or its permission cannot be read), the protection cannot be read, or the protection binds administrators.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B03 — When zero approvals are required, or there is no configuration, the reachability check reports nothing: there is nothing to be unreachable.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B04 — Without the platform CLI the reachability check reports nothing, so the doctor does not duplicate the finding that already names the missing tool.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B05 — When approvals are required and the current account cannot bypass the protection, the check gives one warning `aprovacao-inalcancavel` on the repository, carrying the required count. An administrator with an escape gets no finding: the escape is the expected way around.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B06 — The warning names both ways out: a service account for the agents, or zero required approvals in the configuration applied by the doctor's fix.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-B07 — `DisableApprovalRequirement`: Turning the requirement off replaces the branch protection on the platform with zero required approving reviews and no enforcement on administrators, sending the new protection as the request body.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-I01 — The reachability warning and the bypass answer agree: the warning appears exactly when the bypass is refused.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-X01 — The reachability check only READS the platform: it never changes the branch protection.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-E01 — The platform refuses the protection update.](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

- [APRCP-E02 — REF[APRCP-B02]: an unreadable answer of the platform while deciding the bypass is a refusal with its reason, not an error](layers/infra.md#aprcp--approvalreachable--the-doctor-says-when-the-required-approval-can-never-be-given-and-how-to-get-out)

### [GHEGT — GitHubEnvironment — the doctor warns, before the work starts, about the pieces the GitHub flow silently needs](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B01 — Outside GitHub mode, or with no configuration, nothing is checked.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B02 — Each flow pipeline missing on disk gives a warning `pipeline-ausente` on its file, saying what stops happening and pointing at the doctor's fix.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B03 — A pipeline present without serialization gives its own warning `pipeline-sem-serializacao`, saying the same card can reach two agents; it is never reported as missing.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B04 — A pipeline that still carries the template marker and differs from the current template gives a warning `pipeline-desatualizado`; one whose marker the team removed is not reported.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B05 — When the branch protection cannot be read (the platform answers that there is none), the finding is a warning `main-sem-protecao` on the repository saying a direct push skips the card, the review and the pipeline.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B06 — A branch protection that exists but does not require pull request reviews gives the same check with the "partially protected" message.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B07 — Without the platform CLI, the branch protection is not asked and gives no finding: another finding already names the missing tool.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-B08 — The branch whose protection is read is the declared integration branch (`main` when none is declared), and the finding's message names it.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-I01 — What the doctor charges for pipelines and what its fix seeds come from the same list: after seeding, no pipeline finding remains.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-X01 — The project board is not checked, and no finding mentions it.](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

- [GHEGT-E01 — REF[GHEGT-B05]: a failed read of the branch protection is the answer for an unprotected branch, so it becomes the finding, not an error](layers/infra.md#ghegt--githubenvironment--the-doctor-warns-before-the-work-starts-about-the-pieces-the-github-flow-silently-needs)

### [GVOPG — GovernanceOpportunities — the doctor suggests the canonical gates and settings a project has not adopted yet](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B01 — A map with both test and code nodes and no gate named `evidence-fresh` gives an informational `sugestao-gate` on `evidence-fresh`.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B02 — A map with code and no gate named `no-secret-leaked` gives an informational `sugestao-gate` on `no-secret-leaked`.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B03 — When `no-secret-leaked` is declared but does not block, the finding is an informational `gate-subotimo` on it instead of a suggestion.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B04 — A map with code gives an informational `sugestao-gate` for `dependency-vulnerable` and for `no-duplication`, each when that gate is not declared.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B05 — A map with test nodes where no test suite declares JUnit output gives an informational `config-subotima` on `tests.junit`.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B06 — A nil map or a nil configuration gives no finding.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B07 — `QuickGovernanceHints`: The quick hints are the first two opportunities in order, or all of them when there are fewer, leaving out a catalog suggestion whose gate presupposes a field the project has not declared — the doctor still lists it.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-B08 — Every catalog gate that relates to a declared layer and that the project does not declare, beyond the ones above, is an informational `sugestao-gate` on it, saying what it measures, how to declare it, and the field it presupposes when it has one.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-I01 — Every opportunity is informational: this unit never raises a warning.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

- [GVOPG-X01 — A gate the project already declares (blocking, for the secret gate) is never suggested again, and a project with JUnit output is not told to add it.](layers/infra.md#gvopg--governanceopportunities--the-doctor-suggests-the-canonical-gates-and-settings-a-project-has-not-adopted-yet)

### [DCTRO — Doctor — the global health check that hunts the systemic loose ends of a project](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B01 — `Diagnose`: The diagnosis runs every check and returns the findings sorted by check and then by subject, with the number of nodes, edges and declared layers.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B02 — The warnings of a report are only its findings of warning severity, in order.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B03 — A node whose file is missing on disk is a warning `no-fantasma`.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B04 — An edge whose source or target is not a node of the map is a warning `aresta-morta` on "source → target".](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B05 — A spec that is the source of no edge is a warning `spec-sem-realizacao`: a requirement with no incarnation.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B06 — A spec without an identity code is a warning `identidade-ausente`.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B07 — A code owned by units of DIFFERENT domains is a warning `identidade-duplicada` on the code, naming the owning units. A domain is the `features/<name>` segment of the path, or its top directory outside `features/`.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B08 — Units of the same domain sharing one code are deliberate and give no finding.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B09 — Only specs, features, tests and code own a code; documents, guides and plans only reference it and never collide.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B10 — The files of one unit (its spec, feature, test and code, same folder and name) count as one owner.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B11 — A file that declares its codes as shared (`@anchors-shared-code`) is not an owner of them.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B12 — A declared layer with no node of its kind is a warning `camada-vazia`.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B13 — A guide that is the source of no `governs` edge is a warning `guide-sem-governo`.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B14 — A spec, feature or test kind present in the map that no gate confronts is a warning `kind-sem-gate`; code and documents may legitimately have no gate of their own.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B15 — A perspective in a gate's `skip_on` other than `change` or `all` is a warning `skip-on-invalido` on the gate, quoting the value.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B16 — A gate whose required tool is not on the PATH is a warning `ferramenta-ausente` on the gate, carrying its install hint when there is one.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B17 — Without the git binary, the warning `git-ausente` is on `git` and asks to install it, never to initialize a repository.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B18 — With git but no repository, the warning `git-ausente` asks to initialize one, and does not point at the PATH.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B19 — A `.git` in the root or in any ancestor counts as a repository, whether it is a folder or a file (a worktree or submodule pointer).](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B20 — In GitHub mode the missing repository's text says the work queue has nowhere to come from.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B21 — A plan whose `needs` names a plan that does not exist is a warning `needs-quebrado` on it, naming the missing target.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B22 — A cycle of `needs` between plans gives one warning `needs-ciclo` on a plan of the cycle, whose path names only the cycle's plans, closing on the first; plans are walked in path order, so the same map always gives the same finding.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B23 — A chain of needs in order, or a project without plans, gives no finding.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B24 — Tests in the map with no ingested result at all, and code with no ingested coverage at all, are each a warning `sinal-ausente`. One node with the signal is enough.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B26 — Tests with no result when a JUnit report WAS ingested — the specs hold scenarios it proved — are the warning that the report reached no test file, saying the report names no file the map knows and how to make it; with no report ingested, the warning is the one to run the ingest.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B27 — A declared gate whose `presupposes` names a field the project neither declares nor waives in `dialect.opt_out` is a warning `premissa-ausente` on the gate, naming the field and how to declare or waive it.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-B25 — Code with no mutation signal is an informational `sinal-ausente`; code where only some files have it is an informational `sinal-ausente` on the partial mutation, carrying how many of how many.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-I01 — A project with nothing wrong gives the doctor no warning: each check that finds nothing adds nothing.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

- [DCTRO-X01 — Code without a spec is never reported.](layers/infra.md#dctro--doctor--the-global-health-check-that-hunts-the-systemic-loose-ends-of-a-project)

### [PNDCP — PendingDecisions — the doctor lists the specs that still hold open decisions, the heaviest first](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-B01 — A spec with open decisions gives one warning `decisao-pendente` on that spec, carrying how many decisions are open.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-B02 — A spec that closed its open decisions section with "none" is not pending and gives nothing.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-B03 — The findings are ordered by count, the spec with the most open decisions first.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-B04 — A nil map, or a map with no open decision anywhere, gives no finding; nodes that are not specs are not read.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-I01 — The count the doctor reports for a spec is the count the check's open decisions rule reads from the same text.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-X01 — The unit does not decide what an open decision is: it delegates the count to the check's rule.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

- [PNDCP-E01 — A spec node's file cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#pndcp--pendingdecisions--the-doctor-lists-the-specs-that-still-hold-open-decisions-the-heaviest-first)

### [SPSCS — SpecSections — the doctor tells when most specs of a layer lack a section a gate needs to see](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B01 — Six sections are recommended: navigation, data contract, data states, test identifiers, domain and states; a screen spec with none of them and no gate declared is told about all six.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B02 — A section is reported only when it is missing in MORE than half of the specs it applies to; exactly half, or a minority, is silent.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B03 — When the gate that confronts the section is declared, the finding is a warning `secao-ausente`: the gate is declared and blind.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B04 — When the section's gate is not declared, the finding is an informational `secao-recomendada`, and its text also asks to declare that gate.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B05 — A section title counts in any supported language and in any case.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B06 — The layer of a spec is the one its header declares, over the map's layer.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B07 — A section scoped to other layers is not demanded: a spec of business logic is not asked for navigation, test identifiers, data contract, data states or states.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B08 — The findings are one per section, never one per spec, each carrying how many specs lack it out of how many it applies to.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-B09 — A nil map or configuration gives no finding.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-I01 — Adding the section that was reported to the specs removes the finding: presence and absence are read by the same titles.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-X01 — The unit never reports a spec file by name: it aggregates per section.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

- [SPSCS-E01 — A spec node's file cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#spscs--specsections--the-doctor-tells-when-most-specs-of-a-layer-lack-a-section-a-gate-needs-to-see)

### [ARCHR — ArtifactChoice — turns the artifacts the user chose at init into artifact layers and colocation](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B01 — The artifact options (`ArtifactNames`) are spec, feature, test, guide, plan and code (`CodeArtifact`), in that order.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B02 — Each artifact inference found is pre-checked — code when inference found a code directory — and no other artifact is.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B03 — Applying the choice (`ApplyArtifactChoice`), a chosen artifact whose layer does not exist gets one, even when nothing was detected, with the artifact's kind, its default pattern and its name as tag.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B04 — An artifact that was not chosen loses its layer, and code layers are left as they are.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B05 — A chosen artifact whose layer already exists keeps it as declared.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B06 — The guide and plan layers take the detected folder when there is one, and the default pattern otherwise.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B07 — Colocation (`ApplyColocation`) is declared with the spec as anchor, the chosen code, feature and test beside it, and the spec is never a derivative.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B08 — No colocation is declared when it is not wanted, when the spec is not chosen, or when nothing derives from the spec.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B09 — Choosing code creates no layer and leaving it out removes none: the code layers stay as inference and the user left them.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B10 — Colocation writes only its own part of `derived` (the anchor and the file templates): the rest — the test handle the inference found — is kept, with colocation on and off.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B11 — A test layer created by the choice takes the project's test pattern when one is given (BLCNB-B08), and the default `**/*.test.*` otherwise.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-B12 — The colocated test template is the project's when one is given (BLCNB-B06), and `{{dir}}/{{name}}.test.{{ext}}` otherwise.](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-I01 — REF[ARCHR-B07]: the spec is the anchor of every colocation this unit declares, and never one of its derivatives](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

- [ARCHR-X01 — REF[ARCHR-B04]: code layers are outside this unit; the choice of which code layers to keep belongs to the init decisions (INDCN-B02)](layers/infra.md#archr--artifactchoice--turns-the-artifacts-the-user-chose-at-init-into-artifact-layers-and-colocation)

### [BLCNB — BuildConfig — builds the configuration that inference proposes as the default for the init questions](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B01 — Each detected code directory becomes a code layer named (`LayerNameFor`) after the directory's last segment with the `-code` suffix, tagged with that name; folders sharing that segment are named by their whole path with `-` for `/`, and the root is `root-code`.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B02 — The pattern of a code layer covers its directory recursively, or only the folder's own files when another code directory sits beneath it (the root always): one detected extension is written alone, several are written as a set.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B03 — A proposed code layer excludes specs, features and test files, the test files by the project's test conventions (INPRN-B12), its family's default convention when it has no test yet, and `**/*.test.*` when neither is known.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B04 — Colocation is proposed only when inference detected it, anchored on the spec, with a template only for the derivative kinds inference found (feature, test); the spec is never among the templates.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B05 — The test handle is proposed only when inference found one, with or without colocation; with none found, no default handle is written.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B06 — The colocated test template is where the project's most followed test convention puts a unit's test beside its code (`{{dir}}/{{name}}_test.go`, `{{dir}}/test_{{name}}.py`); with no convention known it is `{{dir}}/{{name}}.test.{{ext}}`.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B07 — The proposal's dialect is the language family inference found (INPRN-B11); with no family, no dialect is written.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-B08 — The test layer's pattern (`TestPattern`) is the project's test convention, several written as a set, its family's default with no test yet, and `**/*.test.*` when neither is known.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-I01 — REF[BLCNB-B05]: a proposal never carries a test handle the project does not use](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [BLCNB-X01 — The proposal creates no artifact layer and no governs rule.](layers/infra.md#blcnb--buildconfig--builds-the-configuration-that-inference-proposes-as-the-default-for-the-init-questions)

- [INDCN-B01 — The code layer names (`CodeLayerNames`) are listed sorted, and only layers of kind code are listed.](layers/infra.md#indcn--initdecisions--the-pure-decisions-of-init-over-the-proposed-configuration-code-layers-tags-and-governs-rules)

### [DFGTD — DefaultGates — the gates a project is born with, by artifact and by project age, and the canonical gate catalog](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B01 — A project with no artifact chosen is seeded with no gate, new or existing.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B02 — A project with spec, feature and test is born with the gates of each, among them the spec completeness, feature non-emptiness, green tests, line coverage and scenario coverage gates.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B03 — The gates that cross spec and feature (spec-feature match, feature-spec match and scenario coverage) are seeded only when both are chosen, and the test-feature match only when test and feature are both chosen.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B04 — Choosing only guides seeds only the guide checklist gate.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B05 — The parent gate is seeded when spec, plan or code is chosen, and confronts exactly the chosen ones among them.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B06 — In an existing project every gate is born informative, except two born blocking by nature: the leaked-secret and the contracted-document gates.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B07 — In a new project every gate is born blocking, except the gates that read an ingested report.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B08 — A gate that reads an ingested report (tests, coverage, mutation, scenario coverage, and the external-tool checks) stays informative even in a new project.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B09 — Every judgment gate that asks about the code or a test carries the @TBD instruction; the one that asks about the proof of a permanent test waiver does not.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B10 — The canonical declaration of a gate is found by name in the catalog of every artifact, including gates seeded only for guides or plans; an unknown name is not found.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B11 — Loading a configuration completes a canonical gate declared by name alone with the catalog's declaration.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B12 — The gate is of the BLOCKING class: a new project is born with it blocking, and an existing one takes it through the same maturation as every structural gate — informative until the project promotes it. It never depends on an ingested signal, so it can block from day one.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B13 — Choosing every artifact `anchors init` offers (ARCHR-B01) seeds every gate of the catalog, the code gates included.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B14 — The gates that run on specs, features and tests — documentation, doctrine, flags, failures, the way back of the unit, the contracted document and the justified change — are seeded without plans; the justified-change gate then runs on specs alone, and the gates that run only on plans are not seeded.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B15 — The gate names registered for the vocabulary check (`RegisterGateNames`) are the full catalog, in catalog order.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B16 — Choosing specs seeds `header-valid`, informative, on every kind Anchors governs — spec, feature, code, test, guide, doc, plan, product and flag —: every governed file carries the `@anchors` header. A bare `- name: header-valid` in a configuration inherits that `on:`.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B17 — `no-duplication` is seeded as the native `duplication` check on code files, needing `npx`: one verdict per file read from jscpd's report, not a project-wide command judged by its exit code.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B18 — The mock gates name the field each one reads: `mock-detect-covers-dialect` and `mock-stamped` presuppose `derived.mock_detect`, `mock-typed` presupposes `derived.mock_contract`; where it is not declared nothing is asked or measured (GTENG-B29), and the doctor names it (DCTRO-B27).](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B19 — `rule-fulfilled` is judged and also marked to review: the marks it judges were put by the agents who wrote the code, and a second look is a different thing from their judgment.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B20 — The catalog carries the checkers that measure a kind of the unit and had no canonical gate — among them `evidence-fresh`, `feature-test-match`, `rule-implemented`, `scenario-identity`, `scenario-letter-declared`, `placeholder-filled` and `updated-at-atual` — each on the kinds it measures, with the field it presupposes when it needs one (`scenario-type-aligned` the `rule_types` tags), and the UI ones scoped by the `screen` and `component` tags.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-B21 — Init seeds (`SeedFor`) the default gates related to the project — a declared layer of a kind they measure, with their tags, or a kind the project chose and has no layer of yet — whose presupposed fields the configuration declares; a gate over an undeclared field is not seeded.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-I01 — The list of seeded gates, and its order, does not change with the age of the project; only the maturation state does.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-I02 — Every gate of the full catalog has a unique name, and its id is its name.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-I03 — Every name the format migration renames a legacy gate to, followed through the later steps that rename it again, is a gate of the full catalog.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-I04 — Choosing plans adds only gates that run on plans.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-X01 — No default gate carries a legacy name.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

- [DFGTD-X02 — No default gate writes Portuguese into the project: its question, measure and install hint are English.](layers/infra.md#dfgtd--defaultgates--the-gates-a-project-is-born-with-by-artifact-and-by-project-age-and-the-canonical-gate-catalog)

### [BREXB — BoardExposure — hand the local board the same page and the same collect contract the pipeline publishes](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B01 — The board page (`BoardHTML`) handed to the local board is byte for byte the page the pipeline publishes.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B02 — The collect expression (`BoardCollectJQ`) handed to the local board is the array expression of the pipeline's collect step, with its card fields and the filter that drops discarded cards, and without surrounding whitespace.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B03 — The collect expression is found both in the direct query shape and in the slurp over the paged raw file, and it ends where the array and the shell quote close, before the output redirection.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B04 — The page counts as active each agent that owns an open card touched within the 30 minutes before the moment the board was taken, the edge included, with how many of its open cards it owns; a released card has no owner and a closed card is not counted.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B05 — On a live board the page counts the 30-minute window from now, not from the moment stamped on the board.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B06 — The page shows one chip per active agent, sorted by name, plus a chip for all agents, or a quiet line when nobody is active; selecting an agent shows only that agent's cards, and selecting none shows every card.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B08 — With no card waiting for a person the blocked strip is hidden and empty.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B09 — The strip lists the cards waiting for a person, the one that blocks more cards first, saying how many cards each blocks and how many wait, with the title stripped of its code prefix; a card that is itself waiting for a person is not counted as blocked.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B10 — A card escalated to a person enters the strip whatever its work state, and the strip says the state it stopped in unless that state is to-do.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B12 — The strip escapes the card titles, so markup in an issue title is shown as text and never run.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B13 — In the columns, an escalated card, and only it, carries a class of its own and a badge saying it waits for you.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B14 — Clicking a card's label in the roadmap opens its details, as a click on a card does in the other tabs.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B15 — A blocked card shows a badge with the number of the card that blocks it, which leads to that card, in a color defined for the light palette and for both dark ones.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-B16 — The cards waiting for a person are split into those that ask a decision and those that ask only framing, and the framing list says how to send a card back to to-do.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-I01 — The extracted expression never carries the shell's output redirection: it opens and closes an array and names no output file.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

- [BREXB-I02 — Every data attribute the page's handlers look for is written by one of its renders, and every data attribute a render writes is looked for by a handler.](layers/infra.md#brexb--boardexposure--hand-the-local-board-the-same-page-and-the-same-collect-contract-the-pipeline-publishes)

### [GTSTG — GitState — classify the project's versioning before `init` scans it, and say what to do about it](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B01 — When git is not installed, the classification (`DetectGit`) is "not installed", whatever the folder holds.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B02 — When git is installed and neither the root nor any ancestor folder has a repository, the state is "not initialised".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B03 — A repository whose local branches hold at least one reference is "ready".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B04 — A repository whose references were packed (no loose branch reference, a non-empty packed list) is "ready".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B05 — A repository with no branch reference and no non-empty packed list is "no commit yet".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B06 — A root inside an existing repository (the repository is in an ancestor folder) is "ready", so no nested repository is ever offered.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B07 — A root whose repository marker is a file (a worktree or a submodule pointer) is "ready".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B08 — There is an action to offer (`OfferAction`) only for "not initialised" (initialise) and "no commit yet" (commit); never for "not installed" or "ready".](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B09 — Each of the three unready states has its own warning (`AvisoGit`), in the project's language — install git, the folder is not under git, there is no commit yet — and "ready" has none.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-B10 — The seeded ignore list covers the system clutter and the Anchors working area, with no exception inside that area and nothing that guesses the stack.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-I01 — "Not installed" and "not initialised" are never merged: the same empty folder gives the two different states depending only on whether git is installed, and only one of them has something to offer.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-X01 — Does not guess the project's stack in the seeded ignore list.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [GTSTG-X02 — Does not look up the git program itself; the caller says whether it is installed.](layers/infra.md#gtstg--gitstate--classify-the-projects-versioning-before-init-scans-it-and-say-what-to-do-about-it)

- [HDGDH-I01 — The guide seeded in any supported language is recognised by the compliance-section heading the `guide-checklist` gate looks for, with at least one checkable point.](layers/infra.md#hdgdh--headerguide--render-the-projects-header-guide-in-the-languages-comment-dialect-passing-the-gate-that-init-itself-declares)

### [INPRN — InferProposal — walks the project and proposes its structure deterministically, for init to confirm](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B01 — Dependency, build and tool directories are not walked: node_modules, .git, dist, build, vendor, .next, coverage, .expo and .anchors.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B02 — The presence of specs, features and tests is detected from their file names.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B03 — A markdown file in a plans folder is a plan, even inside a guides folder, and the first plans folder found is recorded.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B04 — The first guides folder found is recorded, with every guide file found, sorted.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B05 — Every folder holding code is a candidate code directory — the code file's folder cut at two segments, or the root for a file at the root — with no minimum count, ordered by volume, ties by name.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B06 — The code extensions are the five most frequent, most frequent first, ties by name.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B07 — Colocation is detected when at least three stems pair code with a spec, test or feature in the same place.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B08 — The test handle is the known marking attribute used most, only from five uses; on a tie, the earlier attribute of the known list wins.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B09 — The proposal carries the configuration built from it, with code layers and no artifact layer.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B10 — A test named by any convention inference knows (`_test.go`; `.test` and `.spec` with `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`; `_test.py` and `test_*.py`; `_spec.rb` and `_test.rb`; `Test.java`, `Tests.java`, `Test.kt`, `Tests.cs`, `Test.cs`, `Test.php`) has the stem of the code it tests, so `foo_test.go` pairs with `foo.go` and `test_foo.py` with `foo.py` for colocation.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B11 — The language family is the one a manifest at the root declares — `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, checked in that order — or, with no manifest, the family of the most frequent code extension; with neither, there is no family.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-B12 — The test conventions are the naming forms the project's test files follow, most followed first, ties by name; a file follows the longest form it ends with (`.spec.tsx` before `.tsx`).](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-I01 — REF[INPRN-B01]: nothing under a skipped directory ever reaches the proposal, whatever it holds](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-I02 — The same tree always gives the same code extensions, code directories and layer patterns, ties included.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-X01 — Only the first three hundred code files are read in search of the test handle.](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

- [INPRN-E01 — The project root cannot be walked (it does not exist or cannot be read).](layers/infra.md#inprn--inferproposal--walks-the-project-and-proposes-its-structure-deterministically-for-init-to-confirm)

### [INCTN — InitCatalogs — the language dialect catalog and the @TBD instruction that init seeds into judgment gates](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B04 — The @TBD instruction, in English like the question it closes, tells the judge not to answer `pass`, to answer `waived` naming the absence, and it names the piece the gate asks about.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B06 — A file is a test (`testConventionOf`) when its name starts with a convention's prefix and ends with its suffix and has more than both; it follows the first such convention of the catalog.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B07 — A convention's glob (`Glob`) is `**/` with its prefix, `*` and its suffix; its template (`Template`) is `{{dir}}/` with its prefix, `{{name}}` and its suffix.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B08 — A test file's unit name is its name without the convention's prefix and suffix.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B10 — A family's coverage hint (`CoverageHint`) says how its test runner emits the JUnit and lcov reports `anchors ingest` reads; a family with no hint, or no family, gets none.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)
