- [INCTN-B11 — A family's gate script example (`GateScriptExample`) is how a gate step that does more than call one tool runs in the family's own language (`go run ./tools/gates <gate>` for go, `node tools/gates.mjs <gate>` for ts, `python -m tools.gates <gate>` for python); a family with no example gets the generic advice of a program in the project's own language.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-B09 — With no test convention read from the project, the conventions are its family's default; with neither, there are none and no template.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-I02 — The @TBD instruction always demands checking that the declaration is still true, so a stale declaration is reported rather than obeyed.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-I03 — No convention of the catalog is shadowed: a convention whose prefix and suffix also end another listed later is never reached first by a shorter one, so `.spec.tsx` is read as `.spec.tsx`, not `.tsx`.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-I04 — Every family default is one of the catalog's conventions, of that family.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

- [INCTN-X02 — The catalog names no folder: no convention, default or manifest carries a directory.](layers/infra.md#inctn--initcatalogs--the-language-dialect-catalog-and-the-tbd-instruction-that-init-seeds-into-judgment-gates)

### [OPDTP — OperatorDetection — tell whether a person or an AI is running `init`, and whether the discovery phase is still to be done](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B01 — A known agent variable in the environment makes the operator an AI (`DetectOperator`), even when there is a terminal.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B02 — The generic agent variable `AI_AGENT` makes the operator an AI, even when there is a terminal, although it names no tool.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B03 — With no terminal and no agent variable, the operator is an AI.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B04 — With a terminal and no agent variable, the operator is a person.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B05 — The tool (`AgentName`) is named after the known agent variable that is set; with none set the name is empty.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B06 — When several known agent variables are set, the one whose variable name sorts first names the tool, so the same environment always gives the same name.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B07 — The discovery phase is due (`PrecisaDescobrir`) only when the inference found no code folder, spec, feature or test AND there is no project description at the root; a missing proposal counts as nothing found.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B08 — The project description is recognised (`HasProjectMD`) under the spellings `PROJECT.md`, `project.md` and `Project.md`.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B09 — The command that opens the AI (`CommandToOpenAI`) exists only for Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Aider (Aider takes the prompt as a message option); for any other tool, or none, there is no command.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-B10 — The discovery prompt points at `anchors guide project` for the interview and back at `anchors init` for the next step, instead of summarising the interview.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-I01 — The command to open the AI is a list of arguments whose last element is the whole discovery prompt, verbatim — never a shell line the prompt was pasted into.](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

- [OPDTP-X01 — Does not offer a command for a recognised tool whose command-line invocation is not stable (Cursor, Codex).](layers/infra.md#opdtp--operatordetection--tell-whether-a-person-or-an-ai-is-running-init-and-whether-the-discovery-phase-is-still-to-be-done)

### [PCSDP — PackSeeding — copy the compliance packs carried in the binary into the project, never over an adapted one](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-B01 — Seeding (`SeedPacks`) copies every pack the binary carries to `packs/<domain>/<file>` in the project, byte for byte, whatever jurisdiction the project declared.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-B02 — A pack file that already exists in the project is left untouched and reported as preserved, not as created.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-B03 — The lists of created and of preserved packs come back sorted.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-B04 — The list of available packs (`AvailablePacks`) groups them by domain, each named `<domain>/<name>` without the file extension, and each group is sorted.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-I01 — Seeding twice is the same as seeding once: the second run creates nothing and reports every pack as preserved.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-X01 — Does not decide which packs the project adopts; presence on disk is not adoption.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

- [PCSDP-E01 — The pack folders or files cannot be written in the project.](layers/infra.md#pcsdp--packseeding--copy-the-compliance-packs-carried-in-the-binary-into-the-project-never-over-an-adapted-one)

### [INQSN — InitQuestions — describe the human decisions of `init` so an agent can answer them without the terminal UI, and judge every answer](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B01 — The questions are, in this order: header, contributing, artifacts, gates, colocation, layers, workflow, repo, labels, governs.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B02 — Every question carries its identifier, its text, its answer type and what the answer changes; every single-choice question carries its options.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B03 — The defaults come from the inference: the artifacts detected on disk (in name order), whether the project is colocated, and the code layers of the inferred configuration as both the options and the default of the layers question; with no proposal or no configuration, those defaults are empty.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B04 — The work queue is chosen among `local`, `manual` and `github`, `local` by default.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B05 — The verdict (`ValidateAnswers`) has one entry per question, in the questions' order; an answer not given takes the question's default and is marked as default.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B06 — An answer outside the question's options is refused, and the verdict lists the accepted values; a multiple-choice question with no declared options accepts any value.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B07 — In `github` mode, a missing or empty repository and a missing or empty label list are each refused.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B08 — Outside `github` mode, a repository answer is refused.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B09 — A single refused answer makes the whole set refused (`TudoAceito`).](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B10 — An answer given empty is a decision, not the default: it is kept as given and not marked as default.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B11 — The artifacts question offers exactly the artifact options (ARCHR-B01), code included, so an answer of code is accepted.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-B12 — The question texts, their reasons and the refusal details are written in the project's language.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-I01 — Every answer in the set shows up in the verdict, so an answer that was not understood can never pass as accepted in silence.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-X01 — Does not correct an invalid answer to a valid one.](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-E01 — REF[INQSN-B06]: an answer outside the options is the input failure B06 refuses, with the accepted values](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

- [INQSN-E02 — REF[INQSN-B07]: `github` mode without a repository or labels is the dependency failure B07 refuses](layers/infra.md#inqsn--initquestions--describe-the-human-decisions-of-init-so-an-agent-can-answer-them-without-the-terminal-ui-and-judge-every-answer)

### [FLWRF — FlowWorkflows — declare the pipelines of the work flow, find what is missing or broken, and seed them without taking over what the team owns](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B01 — Every pipeline in the flow's list has a carried template and a role, and every one requires serialization except the gates and the board pipelines.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B02 — A pipeline is reported missing (`MissingWorkflow`) only when its file is absent from the pipelines folder; any content counts as present.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B03 — A present pipeline (`SemConcurrency`) that requires serialization and lacks either the concurrency block or the refusal to cancel the run in progress is flagged; absent files and pipelines that need no serialization are never flagged.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B04 — Seeding (`SemeiaWorkflows`) writes every missing pipeline, rewrites every one that still carries the marker with the current template, and returns the names it wrote, sorted.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B05 — Seeding leaves a pipeline without the marker (`ÉTemplateIntacto` is false) untouched and does not list it as written.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B06 — Seeding also writes the board page, outside the pipelines folder, carrying the marker.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B07 — The board page seeding reports "created" when there was no page, "updated" when Anchors' own page differed, and "unchanged" when the page was identical or belongs to the team.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B08 — A pipeline is outdated (`OutdatedWorkflows`) when it still carries the marker and its content differs from the template as seeding would write it now; team-owned and absent pipelines are never outdated.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B09 — Every template line marked as the integration branch becomes a branch list with the project's integration branch — `main` when none is declared — keeping its indentation; this holds for `main` too, so no template's own branch survives the seeding.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B10 — Anchors writes the board columns (`ColumnsAnchorsWrites`) only from TO DO up to READY TO TEST.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B11 — A per-card label (`LabelSob`, `LabelDesbloqueia`, `LabelDePR`, `LabelBlockedBy`) is its prefix followed by the card.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B12 — The stale pipeline releases an owned in-progress card with no progress within its window by commenting the release with the previous owner, which it reads per card, never from the card list; it never releases a card already released, and it skips and names a card whose comments cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B13 — A to-do card whose owner came back from a rejected review is released after the rework window, shorter than the waiting window of an ordinary to-do card.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B14 — The review job publishes the review status of the pull request's card: success or failure on the last approved or rejected verdict line of the reviewer who owned the card when it moved to review, posted after that move, at the start of a line and outside a code block, by someone with write access; pending otherwise, awaiting a reviewer when the card is back in ready-to-review; and no status for a pull request that declares no card or whose card was never moved to review.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B15 — The review job runs on pull request comments that carry a verdict line and may publish statuses, and the mover runs after it, even when it failed or was skipped, never on a comment, receiving its outcome.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B16 — A merge moves the card to ready-to-test, and when the review status was not success it also says on the card that the pull request merged without the review outcome, naming the reviewer and the status, or saying no reviewer had been assigned.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B17 — When a green pull request moves its card to ready-to-review, the review status is published as pending, awaiting a reviewer.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B18 — The claim teaches the reviewer to post the approved or rejected verdict line, and never to move the card on approval.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B19 — An approved or rejected verdict releases the reviewer's ownership of the card, once; a review with no verdict releases nothing.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B20 — When the pull request body references one card and closes another, the review status and the move at the merge are for the closed card.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-B21 — A rejected verdict sends the card back to to-do, owned again by the owner before the reviewer; an approved verdict leaves the card for the merge.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-I01 — What seeding writes is never outdated for the same configuration, whatever the integration branch.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-I02 — The verdict line the review job parses is the one the review guide teaches.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-X01 — Does not take over a file the team owns: a pipeline or a board page without the marker is never rewritten, whatever it holds.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-E01 — The pipelines folder cannot be created.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-E02 — A pipeline cannot be written.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

- [FLWRF-E03 — The binary does not carry a listed template.](layers/infra.md#flwrf--flowworkflows--declare-the-pipelines-of-the-work-flow-find-what-is-missing-or-broken-and-seed-them-without-taking-over-what-the-team-owns)

### [GHIGT — GitHubIssues — the issue lifecycle on the repository's cards, when the project works on GitHub](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B01 — A card is the issue's only when its body holds the key marker exactly, closed by its comment end; a card whose marker merely starts with the key is not it.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B02 — The card title names the gate, what the finding is (per kind) and the target, without the key.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B03 — The card is looked for among open and closed cards (up to 500) by the key, in the configured repository.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B04 — A finding with no card creates one whose body is the issue's body plus the key marker, labelled with the workflow label and the to-do label, and with the needs-user label when the user owns it.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B05 — An assumed debt's card carries only the workflow label, no flow state.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B06 — A finding whose card is open changes nothing: only the search runs.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B07 — A finding whose card is closed reopens it and comments the new report on it.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B08 — Resolving closes the open card with a comment; a card already closed, or none, is left alone.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-B09 — The labels applied are the canonical ones `anchors init` creates, never the legacy Portuguese name.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

- [GHIGT-E01 — A `gh` call fails (search, create, reopen, comment or close), or the search answer is not readable.](layers/infra.md#ghigt--githubissues--the-issue-lifecycle-on-the-repositorys-cards-when-the-project-works-on-github)

### [ISLFS — IssueLifecycle — a divergence recorded so it survives the session, with its state as a folder](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B01 — The key of an issue is its kind, then its gate (when there is one), then its edge (the target, or the anchor, `--vs--` and the target), each path with its slashes turned into hyphens; it does not depend on the date.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B02 — The file name of an issue is its date, two hyphens and its key, with `.md`, and holds no slash.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B03 — The body names the kind and the target in its title and lists the kind, the anchor (when there is one), the target, the gate (when there is one), the owner and the detection date, then the detail under a heading of the kind (left out when the detail brings its own headings).](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B04 — Opening an issue writes it to `todo/`, where the issues of that state are listed by file name (`List`).](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B05 — Opening an issue whose key already exists in any state creates nothing and answers the state it is in, whatever the dates. (`Exists`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B06 — An assumed debt is opened in `future/`, and its body says when it will be paid and that it is an assumed debt. (`OpenAt`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B07 — The body of an open decision closes with how to close it (promote the answer to a rule) and what not to do (delete the item without a rule).](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B08 — Resolving moves a live issue (future, todo or doing) to `done/`; resolving an issue already done, or not found, does nothing. (`Resolve`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B09 — Reopening with a different finding moves the issue to `todo/` and appends the new report under an "Additional finding" heading, keeping the old one; reopening with a finding the issue already holds does nothing.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B10 — An issue with no owner is the agent's, including an issue written before the owner field existed; listing by owner gives only the issues of that owner. (`OwnerOf`, `FileOwner`, `ListByOwner`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B11 — Reassigning changes the owner line of an open issue, keeps the rest of the file (kind included), and appends who it became and why; an issue without an owner line, even with the old Portuguese labels, gets one.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B12 — Reconciling closes every open (todo or doing) violation whose key a full check did not reproduce, and answers the files it closed. (`ReconcileViolations`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-B13 — By default issues are files; configuring GitHub routes the lifecycle to the declared repository's cards. (`UseGitHub`, `UseFiles`)](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-I01 — An issue lives in exactly one state folder: resolving moves it, it never copies it, and a resolved issue is never resurrected by opening it again.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-X01 — Reconciling never closes an issue that is not a violation, nor a violation owned by the user.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-E01 — The state folder cannot be created when an issue is opened.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

- [ISLFS-E02 — The issue to reassign does not exist in the given state.](layers/infra.md#islfs--issuelifecycle--a-divergence-recorded-so-it-survives-the-session-with-its-state-as-a-folder)

### [OBPCB — ObligationPack — distributable sets of obligations from a norm, resolved against the project](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B01 — A pack file gives its name, domain, jurisdiction, authority, required values and obligations, each obligation with the article that originates it.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B02 — A reference ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` is a path (kept when absolute, joined to the project root when relative); any other reference names `packs/<reference>.yaml`.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B03 — Every `{{ name }}` placeholder in an obligation's places is replaced by the project's value for it, spaces inside the braces allowed; the rest of the text is kept. (`LoadAll`)](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B04 — The loaded packs come back sorted by name.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B05 — A pack of a jurisdiction the project does not declare is not loaded, and a warning names the pack and its jurisdiction; jurisdictions are compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-B06 — A global pack, a pack without jurisdiction, or any pack of a project that declares no jurisdictions is loaded.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-E01 — A pack has no name.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-E02 — A pack has no obligations.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-E03 — A pack file is not valid YAML, or does not exist.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

- [OBPCB-E04 — A required value or a placeholder of a pack is not declared by the project.](layers/infra.md#obpcb--obligationpack--distributable-sets-of-obligations-from-a-norm-resolved-against-the-project)

### [TSQUT — TaskQueue — the file-backed queue between "something changed" and "someone works on it"](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B01 — Enqueuing writes the task as `pending__<id>.yaml` in `.anchors/tasks/`, in the pending state. (`Enqueue`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B02 — Enqueuing a task whose target, suggested step and kind are already held by a live (pending or claimed) task creates nothing — and for a judgment the gate must match too, carried by its ID: two judgment gates on one target are two tasks, and a judgment never collapses into a review of another kind.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B03 — Listing gives every live task sorted by ID, taking each task's state from its file name, and nothing when the queue folder does not exist.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B04 — A task whose target file no longer exists is removed from disk when the queue is listed.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B05 — Claiming takes the first pending task, records the worker and the claim moment, and leaves only its claimed file; an empty queue gives no task.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B06 — A pending file whose claimed file already exists (a worker died mid-claim) is not claimed, and it is removed.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B07 — Marking a task done moves it out of the live queue to `.anchors/done/done__<id>.yaml`, after which the same target and step may be enqueued again. (`MarkDone`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B08 — Dropping deletes a live task without writing any history.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B09 — Reclaiming returns to pending, with no worker or moment, every claim older than four hours or with no claim moment; the returned tasks can be claimed again. (`ClaimIsOld`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B10 — Forced reclaiming returns every claimed task, however recent. (`ReclaimForce`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B11 — The count of recently held claims is the number of claimed tasks a reclaim would keep because they are within the window, so a reclaim of zero can explain itself. (`RecentlyHeld`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B12 — The next step suggested for a changed file follows its kind: a draft plan goes to plan review, a plan to spec, a spec to code, code to feature, a feature to test, a test to review, a guide to review (of each unit it governs), and any other kind to triage; every suggestion carries its reason. (`SuggestNext`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B13 — The suggestion for every mapped kind (a draft plan, a plan, a spec, a feature, code, a test, a guide) is a verb `anchors work` can compose; only an unmapped kind gets `triage`, the queue's marker for a step decided by hand. (`ValidWorkArtifact`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B14 — The pending count is the number of live tasks, pending and claimed. (`PendingCount`)](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-B15 — A task whose target is an absolute path is checked at that path, so it is kept while the file exists.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-I01 — A task is never claimed twice, however many workers claim at once.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-X01 — A plain reclaim never returns a claim taken within the last four hours.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-E01 — A task to mark done is neither pending nor claimed.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-E02 — A task to drop is neither pending nor claimed.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-E03 — A task file in the queue is not valid YAML.](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

- [TSQUT-E04 — A task is enqueued under an ID a pending or claimed task already holds (for another target or step).](layers/infra.md#tsqut--taskqueue--the-file-backed-queue-between-something-changed-and-someone-works-on-it)

### [RCDLR — RecodeDialect — the project's own surfaces of a code: testID prefixes and file names](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B01 — The `lower` convention derives the testID prefix as the code in lower case; any other convention derives none. (`TestIDPrefix`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B02 — A testID prefix is rewritten only right after a quote or backtick and when followed by a hyphen and a letter or digit; the number of rewrites is counted. (`RewriteTestIDs`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B03 — With no old prefix, or the same prefix on both sides, the text is left unchanged with zero rewrites.](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B04 — The occurrences of a testID prefix are counted with the same rule, and an empty prefix counts zero. (`CountTestIDPrefix`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B05 — The `testID=` attributes of a text are counted whatever their prefix. (`CountAnyTestID`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B06 — A path matches the project's file patterns for a code when one pattern, with `{{code}}` replaced by the code, matches it; the code is matched with its exact case. (`FileMatchesCode`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-B07 — A file whose name holds the old code on its boundaries (start, dot, hyphen, end) is renamed to the new code in the name only, keeping its folder; a name without it keeps its path. (`RenameFilePath`)](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

- [RCDLR-X01 — Does not rename a file whose name holds a longer code that contains the old one.](layers/infra.md#rcdlr--recodedialect--the-projects-own-surfaces-of-a-code-testid-prefixes-and-file-names)

### [RCPLR — RecodePlan — planning and applying the rename of a code across the whole project](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B01 — A malformed old or new code is refused before anything is read.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B02 — Renaming a code to itself is refused.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B03 — The plan holds, sorted by path, every project file that holds the old code, with its rewritten content; files without the code are left out, and the total counts the content replacements. (`BuildPlan`)](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B04 — With the testID convention declared, the testID prefix derived from the old code is rewritten to the new one, counted apart from the content replacements; without the dialect no testID is touched.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B05 — With file patterns declared, every file whose name matches them for the old code is planned for renaming to the new code; without the dialect no file is renamed.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B06 — When the expected testID prefix appears nowhere but files holding the old code carry testIDs, the plan warns about a divergent prefix and does not rewrite it.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B07 — An old code that appears in no file content, no testID and no file name is refused.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B08 — Applying writes every planned file with its original mode and performs every rename, and answers how many files were written and renamed.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B09 — Inside a repository a tracked file is renamed through git, so the index records the rename; outside a repository it is a plain rename.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B10 — Inside a repository a file git does not track is moved by a plain rename, and a reported success means the file really moved.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B11 — A target code another unit already owns — declared in its header, or the prefix of one of its scenario codes — is refused naming that file; a code that merely contains the target is not a collision.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B12 — The refusal of a malformed code names the lengths the project declares in `code_lengths`, the same ones the validation applies.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B13 — `BuildBatchCited` plans the rename of many codes at once, as a migration makes it: one walk of the governed files, each rewritten once for every code where it is cited as a code (`NewCitedSet`), the files whose names carry a code renamed with it (the given name patterns), the counts per code, and the bare mentions left, per code and file; `Batch.Apply` writes the files and makes the renames as `Plan.Apply` does.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-B14 — A batch never rewrites a binary as text — a file that is not valid UTF-8 or holds a NUL byte, such as a VR baseline —: it is renamed with its code when its name carries one, byte for byte.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-X01 — A refusal from git is returned as an error naming the move, and the file is not moved by other means.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-X02 — Planning writes nothing to the project.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E01 — REF[RCPLR-B01]: a malformed code is refused by B01](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E02 — REF[RCPLR-B02]: the same code on both sides is refused by B02](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E03 — REF[RCPLR-B07]: an old code with nothing to rename is refused by B07](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E04 — REF[RCPLR-X01]: git refusing a move is surfaced by X01](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E05 — A planned file cannot be written while applying.](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

- [RCPLR-E06 — REF[RCPLR-B11]: a target code owned by another unit is refused by B11](layers/infra.md#rcplr--recodeplan--planning-and-applying-the-rename-of-a-code-across-the-whole-project)

### [RCRWR — RecodeRewrite — renaming an identity code inside a text, on every surface where it appears](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B01 — A code is well formed when it is made of upper-case letters and digits and its length is one the project declares. (`ValidCode`)](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B02 — The old code in a `code:` or `ref:` header line is replaced, in the markdown, line-comment and hash-comment header styles alike.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B03 — In a `ref:` list only the old code changes; the other codes of the list stay.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B04 — Every scenario code built on the old code keeps its suffix and takes the new code, and each one counts as one replacement.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B05 — A bare mention of the old code is replaced, the character right after it is kept, and each mention counts as one replacement.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B06 — The dry-run listing classifies each occurrence as a scenario code, a header or a bare reference, counting each occurrence once. (`Find`)](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B07 — Each occurrence in the dry-run listing carries the text it matched and the line it starts on, counted from one, also for headers and mentions that come after scenario codes. (`Find`)](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B08 — `RewriteRuleCodes` rewrites only the rule and scenario codes of OLD — `OLD-B08`, `OLD-S06#02`, `OLD-VR-S01`, `OLD-CT` — and never the bare code, which outside the governed files is as likely an ordinary word or part of an identifier (`DATA_URL`).](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B09 — `RewriteCited` rewrites a code only where it is cited as one — its rule and scenario codes and any name it heads joined by a hyphen (`CODE-DS-method-email`, `CODE-perm-suite`, the stem of a file named by it), the header fields that hold codes (`code:`, `file_code:`, `ref:`/`refs:`, `dep:`, `needs:`), the code in backticks and a Gherkin tag `@CODE` — and leaves the bare word; `CitedSet` (`NewCitedSet`) does it for many codes in one pass over the text (`Rewrite`, and `RewriteRuleCodes` for the rule codes alone) and lists the lines where each still stands bare, an identifier (`CODE_X`, `X_CODE`) not counted.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-B10 — An underscore is no boundary for a bare mention: `CODE_TABLE` and `X_CODE` are identifiers, not mentions of the code, and `Rewrite` leaves them.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-I01 — A text without the old code comes back unchanged with zero replacements, so rewriting a second time after a rewrite changes nothing.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

- [RCRWR-X01 — Never rewrites a longer code that contains the old one, nor a word that merely ends or starts with it.](layers/infra.md#rcrwr--recoderewrite--renaming-an-identity-code-inside-a-text-on-every-surface-where-it-appears)

### [PSXSH — Shell — the POSIX shell that runs a project's commands](layers/infra.md#psxsh--shell--the-posix-shell-that-runs-a-projects-commands)

- [PSXSH-B01 — The shell is the `sh` found on PATH, on every system. (`Path`)](layers/infra.md#psxsh--shell--the-posix-shell-that-runs-a-projects-commands)

- [PSXSH-B02 — On Windows with no `sh` on PATH, the shell is the one beside the installed git: `bin\sh.exe` or `usr\bin\sh.exe` under the root three levels above `git --exec-path`.](layers/infra.md#psxsh--shell--the-posix-shell-that-runs-a-projects-commands)

- [PSXSH-B03 — A command is `sh -c <script>` with the arguments after it as `$0 $1…`. (`Command`)](layers/infra.md#psxsh--shell--the-posix-shell-that-runs-a-projects-commands)

- [PSXSH-E01 — No shell on PATH, and on Windows none beside git either](layers/infra.md#psxsh--shell--the-posix-shell-that-runs-a-projects-commands)

### [TXSMT — TextSimilarity — how close two texts that should be equal are, weighted by what each word discriminates](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B01 — A text is split into upper-cased words on every character that is not a letter or a digit; words of one character and words made only of digits are dropped. (`Tokenize`)](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B02 — The weight of a word is the natural logarithm of the corpus size over the number of texts that contain it, so a word in every text weighs 0. (`Weights`)](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B03 — When no word of the pair carries weight (a homogeneous corpus, such as a single text), both rulers fall back to the unweighted count, so identical texts score 1 and not 0. (`Score`, `Cosine`)](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B04 — Two texts with the same runs of letters and digits in the same order, ignoring case and punctuation, are identical with score 1, before any ruler is applied. Identity reads every run, numbers and one-character words included — unlike the rulers, which read the words of `TXSMT-B01`. (`Classify`)](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B05 — When both rulers reach 0.5, the pair is similar.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B06 — When exactly one of the two rulers reaches 0.5, the pair is borderline.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B07 — When neither ruler reaches 0.5 but the two texts share a rare word (weight of at least 1.38, about a quarter of the corpus or less), the pair is similar.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B08 — Otherwise the pair is divergent.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B09 — The score reported with a non-identical verdict is the larger of the two rulers.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B10 — Texts that differ only by a number are not identical: `radius 9999` against `radius 0`, or `2 rows` against `3 rows`, go on to the rulers, while `123` against `123` is identical with score 1.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B11 — Two texts without any run of letters or digits (`""`, `!!`, `??`) are identical with score 1.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B12 — The two rulers fall back to the unweighted count under the same condition (`TXSMT-B03`); when only one text of the pair has no weighted word, both score 0, so a text made only of words present in the whole corpus is divergent, not borderline. (`Score`, `Cosine`)](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

- [TXSMT-B13 — A verdict's `String` is its English name (`identical`, `similar`, `borderline`, `divergent`), for logs and tests; a user-facing message translates the verdict itself.](layers/infra.md#txsmt--textsimilarity--how-close-two-texts-that-should-be-equal-are-weighted-by-what-each-word-discriminates)

### [SGSTS — SuggestionStore — a proposed fix, as a patch plus its reason, waiting for someone to decide](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B01 — Opening a new suggestion writes it to `suggestions/pending/<ID>.md` with its target as title, the gate, origin, target and proposal date, and the reason under "Why".](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B02 — A suggestion with a patch carries it in a diff block, followed by the command that applies it.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B03 — A suggestion without a patch has no diff block and says the fix is not mechanical and needs a human decision.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B04 — Opening a suggestion whose ID is already pending creates nothing and answers the existing path.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B05 — A suggestion already approved or rejected is never reopened: opening it again creates nothing, and nothing appears in pending.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B06 — Deciding moves the suggestion from pending to approved or rejected, appending a Decision section with the state, the date, who decided and the reason. (`Decide`)](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B07 — A decision taken under automatic judgment is recorded as taken by the AI, distinct from a decision by a person.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B08 — Listing a state gives the IDs of its suggestions, sorted, and nothing (without error) when the state's folder does not exist.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-B09 — The patch of a suggestion is extracted clean, without the diff fences, ready for `git apply`. (`PatchOf`)](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-I01 — A suggestion is in exactly one state folder: once decided, it is no longer pending.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-E01 — A suggestion without an ID is opened.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-E02 — A decision names a state other than approved or rejected.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-E03 — A decision has a blank reason.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-E04 — The suggestion to decide is not pending.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

- [SGSTS-E05 — The patch is asked of a suggestion that has none.](layers/infra.md#sgsts--suggestionstore--a-proposed-fix-as-a-patch-plus-its-reason-waiting-for-someone-to-decide)

### [TSTLS — TestList — the project's tests, read the way the project says they are written](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B01 — With a pattern, each call it opens that is followed by a string literal is a test: the literal is its title, and the line is the line where the call starts.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B02 — A title may be quoted with single quotes, double quotes or backticks; a backslash escapes the next character inside the first two, and only a backtick title may span lines.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B03 — A call whose next token is not a string literal is not a test this reading can name, and is left out.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B04 — The pattern's tests come in file order, then in the order they appear in each file.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B05 — With a script, the command runs at the project root and the tests are what it prints under the contract.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B06 — Output outside the contract is refused, naming what is wrong: not a single JSON object, an unknown field, a version other than 1, no `tests`, an empty or non-relative `file`, a `line` below 1, an `end` before its `line`, or an empty `title`. (`Parse`)](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B07 — A `file` in the script's output is read with forward slashes and without redundant segments, so it matches the map's IDs.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B08 — A source that declares neither a pattern nor a script lists no test and raises no error.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B09 — The script may say where each test ends (`end`, its last line), and the test carries it; a test without `end`, and every test a pattern reads, carries zero — the end is not known.](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-B10 — A pattern scans the test files through the reader given to `ListFrom` — the git index, under `--index` —, and through the tree when none is given. (`ListFrom`)](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-E01 — The source declares both a pattern and a script](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-E02 — The pattern does not compile](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-E03 — The script exits with an error](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

- [TSTLS-E04 — REF[TSTLS-B06]: the script answers outside the contract](layers/infra.md#tstls--testlist--the-projects-tests-read-the-way-the-project-says-they-are-written)

### [RCGRL — RuleCodeGrammar — the grammar that recognizes a scenario code in a test's name, in the project's vocabulary](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B01 — A rule code — the unit's identity, a dash, a declared rule letter and two digits — is recognized in a test's name, wherever it appears in the text.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B02 — A rule code followed by a lowercase slug (`-some-slug`) is recognized with the slug as part of the code.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B03 — A design-system item (`CODE-DS-<name>`) and the visual-regression marker (`CODE-VR`) are recognized as codes.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B04 — `SetRuleLetters`: Declaring the rule letters replaces the vocabulary: a declared letter is recognized, and a letter outside the declaration is not.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B05 — `SetCodeLenPattern`: Declaring the code length replaces the accepted identity length: an identity of a newly declared length is recognized.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B06 — An empty declaration of letters or of length keeps the vocabulary that was in place: a configuration that declares nothing changes nothing.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B07 — A scenario code keeps its variant suffix (`CODE-B02#02`) and its rule is the code without it (`ScenarioRoot`); a feature's scenario tags are read with their variants, each once (`FeatureScenarios`).](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-B08 — A rule is proven when every scenario its features declare is proven — its own code when a scenario carries no variant, each `#NN` when they do; a rule no feature declares a scenario of is proven by its own code or any variant; the declared scenarios of a rule left unproven are named in order. (`RulesProven`, `UnprovenScenarios`)](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-I01 — The default rule letters are the configuration's default rule letters, letter for letter. A report read before the configuration loads recognizes the same rules the rest of the engine does.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

- [RCGRL-X01 — An identity longer than the accepted length, or glued to a longer word, is not a code.](layers/infra.md#rcgrl--rulecodegrammar--the-grammar-that-recognizes-a-scenario-code-in-a-tests-name-in-the-projects-vocabulary)

### [DCLDF — DiffChangedLines — which lines of which files a change added, read from a unified diff](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B01 — Each added line is recorded under the path of the file the preceding new-file header names; removed lines are not recorded.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B02 — A hunk header sets the new-side line number the next added line gets, in both the `+start,count` and the bare `+start` form; a header without a new side gives line 0.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B03 — The `a/` and `b/` prefixes and a tab-separated timestamp after the path are stripped, so the path is the file's path relative to the root.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B04 — A deleted file (new side `/dev/null`) records nothing, and a file left with no added line is dropped from the result.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B05 — Unchanged context lines advance the new-side line number without being recorded.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B06 — `GitDiff`: From git, the working copy is compared against the current commit when no reference is given, and against the reference when one is.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B07 — Inside a hunk, every line up to the counts its header gives is content: an added line whose text starts with `++ ` (it reads `+++ `) is recorded as a line, and a removed line whose text starts with `-- ` is a removal, never a file header.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-B08 — A very long line in the diff, hundreds of kilobytes on one line, is read like any other: it and every line after it are still recorded.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-I01 — Removed lines never shift the new-side numbering: a line added after removals keeps the number its hunk header gives it.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-X01 — `ParseDiffFile`: Reading a diff file needs no git: the file is read as text, wherever it came from.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-E01 — The root is not a git repository, or git fails.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

- [DCLDF-E02 — The diff file cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#dcldf--diffchangedlines--which-lines-of-which-files-a-change-added-read-from-a-unified-diff)

### [JUIJN — JUnitIngest — the run's outcome per test case, and the scenario codes each case proves, read from a JUnit report](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B01 — `ParseJUnit`: A report whose root lists suites is read into one result per case of every suite.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B02 — A report whose root is a single suite is read the same way.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B03 — Suites nested inside suites are flattened: their cases are read as well.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B04 — A case without its own file takes its suite's file; a case that names its file keeps it.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B05 — A case with a failure or an error is failed; a case marked skipped is skipped.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B06 — The proven codes are the codes named by the cases that neither failed nor were skipped.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B07 — The seen codes are the codes named by every case, passed, failed or skipped.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B08 — `CodesInCase`: Every code a case's name mentions is extracted, in the vocabulary the project declared.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B09 — A file that is not a JUnit report is read as a report with no cases: nothing is proven by it.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B10 — Each case carries its run time in seconds from its `time` attribute; a missing, malformed or negative time reads as 0.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B12 — A case naming a visual-regression code of a state — `{CODE}-VR-S01` — also proves (and is seen for) the state it captures, `{CODE}-S01`: a green capture shows the state under its condition, looking as the spec says.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-B11 — The codes a report proves and sees carry the variant a case names (`CODE-B02#02`): a case of one variant never stands for its sibling. (`ScenarioCodesInCase`, `PassedCodes`, `SeenCodes`)](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-I01 — Every proven code is also a seen code: a run cannot prove what it did not measure.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-I02 — A scenario is proven only by a case that ran, passed, and names exactly that scenario: a skipped or failed case proves nothing, and a variant is never proven by its sibling or by its rule.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-X01 — Only the case's name carries codes: a code in the suite's or the class's name proves nothing.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

- [JUIJN-E01 — The report file cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#juijn--junitingest--the-runs-outcome-per-test-case-and-the-scenario-codes-each-case-proves-read-from-a-junit-report)

### [LCINL — LcovIngest — line coverage per file, and the uncovered lines of a change, read from an lcov report](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B01 — `ParseLCOV`: Each record, opened by its source-file line and closed by the end-of-record line, becomes one file's coverage, in report order.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B02 — A line-hit entry with a positive hit count marks that line covered, and one with zero hits marks it uncovered.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B03 — When the record states its line totals, those totals win over the count of line-hit entries.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B04 — The uncovered lines of a change are the changed lines that are instrumented and not covered.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B05 — The instrumented count of a change is the number of changed lines the report instrumented.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B06 — The coverage percentage is covered over total lines times one hundred, and zero when the file has no line.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B07 — A record left without its end-of-record line is closed by the next source-file line or by the end of the report.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B08 — A line-hit entry that carries the optional checksum field is read by its hit count; the checksum does not change whether the line is covered.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B09 — Line-hit and line-total entries before the first source-file line belong to no file and change no file's counts.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-B10 — A branch entry (`BRDA:<line>,<block>,<branch>,<taken>`) records the branch by `<line>:<block>:<branch>`, taken when its count is positive and never taken when it is zero or `-`; an entry with another number of fields, a line that is not a positive number, or before the first source-file line records nothing. A record with no branch entry has no branch.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-I01 — An uncovered changed line is always an instrumented changed line: the uncovered lines never exceed the instrumented count.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-X01 — Only line coverage is read: branch and function entries do not change the line counts.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

- [LCINL-E01 — The report file cannot be opened.](layers/infra.md#lcinl--lcovingest--line-coverage-per-file-and-the-uncovered-lines-of-a-change-read-from-an-lcov-report)

### [MTINM — MutationIngest — the mutation score per file, read from a Mutation Testing Elements report](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B01 — `ParseMutationFormat` reads the canonical format for the names `mutation-testing-elements`, `mte`, `stryker` and the empty name, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; `ParseMutation` reads it with no name given.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B02 — A killed mutant and a timed-out mutant both count as killed. The timed-out are also counted apart, since under load they inflate the score.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B03 — A surviving mutant counts as survived, and its starting line is recorded.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B04 — A mutant no test covered is counted apart and does not enter the score, and its starting line is recorded.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B05 — A mutant the tool ignored is counted apart and does not enter the score.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B06 — A mutant that failed to compile or to run is not counted and does not enter the score.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B07 — The score is killed over killed plus survived, times one hundred; a file where no mutant ran has no score (zero, not written to the map): nothing was measured.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B08 — The low and high thresholds are read from the report when it carries them.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B10 — A report in the format — it carries its schema version — with no file is a run that had nothing to mutate: it is read as a report of no file, not refused.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-B09 — A file's path is normalized: a leading `./` is dropped, and a path containing `/src/` is cut to start at `src/`.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-I01 — A file where nothing ran is told apart from a proven one: it has no score, and its uncovered or ignored mutants stay counted.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-X01 — Thresholds absent from the report stay zero: the unit never invents a threshold.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-E01 — The format name is not one the unit knows.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-E02 — The report is not JSON of the canonical format.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-E03 — The report has no file and no schema version.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

- [MTINM-E04 — The report file cannot be read.](layers/infra.md#mtinm--mutationingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-mutation-testing-elements-report)

### [GRING — GremlinsIngest — the mutation score per file, read from a gremlins report](layers/infra.md#gring--gremlinsingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-gremlins-report)

- [GRING-B01 — The report's listed files are read into one mutation result per file.](layers/infra.md#gring--gremlinsingest--the-mutation-score-per-file-read-from-a-gremlins-report)
